title: Can a Phone Be a Cow? (with Philip Auerswald)
speaker: Russ Roberts

sentences.en: The first episode, with Ido Hevroni of Shalem College, who has been teaching the Iliad for over a decade, will air July 6th.
sentences.zh: 第一期节目将于7月6日播出，嘉宾是夏莱姆学院的伊多·赫夫罗尼，他教授《伊利亚特》已有十多年。

sentences.en: It will provide some useful context on the book to help you get started, and I hope inspire you to read it.
sentences.zh: 这一期会为这本书提供一些有用的背景信息，帮助你入门，也希望能激发你去读一读原著。

sentences.en: Additional episodes--I don't know how many--will air in the weeks to follow, at least one, maybe two.
sentences.zh: 接下来的几周里还会有更多期节目——具体多少我也说不准，至少一期，也许两期。

sentences.en: And, we'll be using the Fagles translation, but there are many others to choose from.
sentences.zh: 我们会采用费格尔斯的译本，不过市面上还有很多其他译本可供选择。

sentences.en: And now for today's guest, economist and author Philip Auerswald of George Mason University.
sentences.zh: 现在请出今天的嘉宾，乔治梅森大学的经济学家兼作家菲利普·奥尔斯瓦德。

sentences.en: Philip was last here in September of 2017 talking about populism.
sentences.zh: 菲利普上次来节目是在2017年9月，当时聊的是民粹主义。

sentences.en: Our topic for today is his latest book with the delightful title, A Phone Is a Cow: How Pioneers of the Mobile Revolution Helped Millions Lift Themselves Out of Poverty.
sentences.zh: 今天的话题是他那本书名很有意思的新书——《手机就是一头牛：移动革命的先驱者如何帮助数百万人摆脱贫困》。

sentences.en: Philip, welcome back to EconTalk. Thanks so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 菲利普，欢迎再次做客EconTalk。非常感谢邀请我。

sentences.en: It's a pleasure. So, let's start with the title of the book.
sentences.zh: 很荣幸。那我们就从书名说起吧。

sentences.en: What does that mean, A Phone Is a Cow? So, A Phone Is a Cow comes from the story of Iqbal Quadir, who is a central figure in the book.
sentences.zh: “手机就是一头牛”是什么意思？这个说法来自伊克巴尔·夸德尔的故事，他是书中的核心人物。

sentences.en: And, Iqbal is the founder of Grameenphone, which is today the dominant provider of mobile telephony services in Bangladesh.
sentences.zh: 伊克巴尔是Grameenphone的创始人，这家公司如今是孟加拉国移动通信服务的主导提供商。

sentences.en: And, Iqbal faced the challenge of creating a mobile phone company in Bangladesh at a time when per capita income in Bangladesh was about $400 a year, which was the same price as a mobile digital handset at the time.
sentences.zh: 伊克巴尔面临的挑战是：他要在孟加拉国创办一家手机公司，而当时孟加拉国的人均年收入大约只有400美元，恰好和当时一部数字手机的价格差不多。

sentences.en: So, it was a daunting undertaking. Iqbal is featured along with Strive Masiyiwa, because they were really the first two people to see mobile phones as a potential device for really everybody, including the rural poor in places like Bangladesh and Zimbabwe.
sentences.zh: 所以这是个令人望而生畏的事业。书里把伊克巴尔和斯特赖夫·马西尤瓦放在一起写，因为他们俩真的是最早意识到手机可以属于每一个人——包括孟加拉国和津巴布韦这类地方的农村穷人——的两个人。

sentences.en: So, Iqbal was trying to understand essentially the business model to make mobile telephony work at the rural level, and he drew inspiration--in fact, partnership--with Grameen Bank.
sentences.zh: 伊克巴尔当时其实是在琢磨怎样设计一套商业模式，让移动通信在农村也能行得通，他从格莱珉银行那里获得了启发——事实上后来还成了合作伙伴。

sentences.en: And, so, Grameen Bank is famously known for micro loans to women in villages to essentially use those loans for productive assets, including, say, a cow.
sentences.zh: 格莱珉银行出名的地方，就是向乡村妇女发放小额贷款，让她们用这些钱购置有生产力的资产，比如说，一头牛。

sentences.en: So, the loan would really pay for itself through the productive use of the asset.
sentences.zh: 这笔贷款会通过这项资产的生产性用途来实现自我偿还。

sentences.en: And, Iqbal's really central insight in terms of making mobile phones viable in a place like Bangladesh in the mid-1990s was that a phone could be a cow.
sentences.zh: 伊克巴尔在上世纪九十年代中期让手机在孟加拉国这样的地方行得通的核心洞见就是：手机也可以是一头牛。

sentences.en: A phone was essentially a productive item, a productive asset, and not, as it really was seen in the West at the time, as a consumption good, a luxury good.
sentences.zh: 手机本质上是一件能产生生产力的东西、一项生产性资产，而不是像当时西方人看待的那样，是一种消费品、一种奢侈品。

sentences.en: So, that's where A Phone Is a Cow comes from.
sentences.zh: “手机就是一头牛”这个说法就是这么来的。

sentences.en: And one of the things I love about this book, we hear his story, which is--to call it a roller coaster doesn't do justice to it.
sentences.zh: 我特别喜欢这本书的一点是，我们能读到他的故事——说这是过山车都不足以形容它的跌宕起伏。

sentences.en: He and the other entrepreneur you mentioned, Strive, overcome unbelievable business hurdles, technical hurdles, regulatory hurdles; but the fundamental hurdle is what you just mentioned.
sentences.zh: 他和你提到的另一位企业家斯特赖夫，克服了难以置信的商业障碍、技术障碍、监管障碍；但最根本的障碍就是你刚才说的那个。

sentences.en: You have a desperately poor country, and you have an item that is a year's worth of income, if not more, for many, many of the people who are going to be the customers.
sentences.zh: 一个极度贫困的国家，一件东西对很多、很多未来的顾客来说，价格相当于一年甚至更多的收入。

sentences.en: So, it's a fool's errand on the surface.
sentences.zh: 表面上看，这简直是件傻子才会做的事。

sentences.en: What's beautiful about it, of course, is that since that gleam in his eye, the price of a cell phone has fallen dramatically, and per capita income in Bangladesh has gone through the roof.
sentences.zh: 当然，美妙之处在于，自从他脑子里冒出那个念头以来，手机价格已经大幅下降，孟加拉国的人均收入也一路飙升。

sentences.en: For Bangladesh, it increased dramatically, let's just say it that way.
sentences.zh: 就孟加拉国来说，这么说吧，涨幅相当惊人。

sentences.en: Yes, yeah. And, the reach of that product is absurd, to the point where now, Bangladesh, even though its per capita income has grown dramatically--it still is not a rich country--but there are more cell phones than there are people in Bangladesh.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。而且这款产品的普及程度简直离谱，如今孟加拉国的手机数量已经超过了人口数量——虽然人均收入涨了很多，它依然算不上一个富裕国家，但情况就是这样。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah. No, I mean, exactly. And, I think one of the things I really loved about delving into Iqbal's story, I mean, he and I have known each other for 20 years, so it was really an opportunity for me to work with him and really understand the details, the particulars of how that came about and situated in this kind of full context.
sentences.zh: 对，对。没错，就是这样。我觉得深入研究伊克巴尔的故事时最让我着迷的一点是——我和他相识已经20年了，所以这也是个难得的机会，能和他一起合作，真正弄清楚事情发生的细节、来龙去脉，并把它放进完整的背景里去理解。

sentences.en: But, one of the details that surfaced was that he and his brother had a previous business idea, which was to develop a Bengali character set for the Macintosh--the earliest Macintosh.
sentences.zh: 但其中浮现出来的一个细节是，他和他哥哥之前还有过一个商业点子，就是为Macintosh——最早期的那款Macintosh——开发一套孟加拉语字符集。

sentences.en: And, at that time, a Macintosh computer cost about $4,000, and the per capita income in Bangladesh was $200.
sentences.zh: 当时一台Macintosh电脑要卖大约4000美元，而孟加拉国的人均收入只有200美元。

sentences.en: So, it was basically roughly 20 to one.
sentences.zh: 所以大致是二十比一的差距。

sentences.en: So, really, the obstacle was seeming completely insurmountable.
sentences.zh: 所以说，这个障碍看起来是完全无法逾越的。

sentences.en: Now, I think perhaps at the time they started Grameenphone, now that I think about it, may have been more like $300.
sentences.zh: 现在回想起来，他们创办Grameenphone的时候，人均收入可能已经涨到了300美元左右。

sentences.en: The handset was $400, so it was a little bit more than one-to-one.
sentences.zh: 手机是400美元，所以差不多刚过一比一。

sentences.en: But, what Iqbal was looking at was not the absolute number, the one-to-one, but it was the change: that it had gone from 20-to-one to one-to-one.
sentences.zh: 但伊克巴尔关注的不是一比一这个绝对数字本身，而是变化趋势：从二十比一变成了一比一。

sentences.en: And, that trend on the cost side, there was every reason to believe that the cost, due to Moore's law, which Iqbal was very well aware, would continue to drop exponentially, and that income would grow.
sentences.zh: 而在成本这一端的趋势，有充分理由相信——伊克巴尔对摩尔定律非常了解——成本会继续呈指数级下降，同时收入也会增长。

sentences.en: And, so, he foresaw exactly the phenomenon that you described, and that was really what the vision for Grameenphone was based on.
sentences.zh: 所以，他准确预见到了你刚才描述的这种现象，Grameenphone的整个构想正是建立在这个基础之上。

sentences.en: But besides the profitability--which ultimately came--there was an idea that this was going to make the world a better place by allowing people to have the freedom to pursue some things they might not otherwise be able to do because they were able to communicate.
sentences.zh: 但除了最终实现的盈利之外，还有一种理念：这件事会让世界变得更美好，因为人们有了通信能力之后，就能自由地去做一些原本做不到的事情。

sentences.en: And, one of the themes of this book is the power of communication and connection between people; also the power of connecting different products together in innovative ways.
sentences.zh: 这本书的主题之一，就是人与人之间沟通与连接的力量；也包括以创新方式将不同产品连接在一起的力量。

sentences.en: But, how did the phone help make the people of Bangladesh more productive?
sentences.zh: 但手机究竟是怎样帮助孟加拉国人民提高生产力的呢？

sentences.en: In other words: It's true that once he had the idea, eventually Bangladesh got much wealthier, and the cost of the cell phone fell, which made it a more viable business proposition.
sentences.zh: 换句话说：确实，他有了这个想法之后，孟加拉国最终变得更富裕了，手机成本也下降了，这让这门生意变得更加可行。

sentences.en: But, the beautiful part of this story is that part of that transition was helped by the phone, because the phone allowed people to do more than just chat with their relatives in far-away places.
sentences.zh: 但这个故事美妙的地方在于，这场转变本身，有一部分正是手机推动的，因为手机能让人们做的事，远不止和远方的亲戚聊聊天。

sentences.en: How is the phone in a poor country more than just a consumer luxury?
sentences.zh: 在一个贫穷国家里，手机为什么不只是一件消费性的奢侈品？

sentences.en: Yeah. I think one of the difficulties of situating this book--particularly in contemporary U.S. discussions about the mobile phone--is that we see the mobile phone not only as a consumer device, but as a pernicious consumer device-- -- A time sink, a distraction engine.
sentences.zh: 是啊。我觉得给这本书定位的难点之一——尤其是在当下美国关于手机的讨论语境里——在于我们不仅把手机看作一种消费设备，还把它看作一种有害的消费设备——是吞噬时间的黑洞，是制造分心的机器。

sentences.en: And, the idea that the mobile phone could be a productivity enhancer seems anachronistic, or, if not just completely made up, right?
sentences.zh: 而“手机能提升生产力”这种说法，听起来像是不合时宜，甚至完全是凭空捏造出来的，对吧？

sentences.en: That's just not our lived experience. But, there's something that you and I, and I think probably everybody else, knows, which is, the United States is not Bangladesh.
sentences.zh: 这就是不符合我们的亲身体验。但有一点，你我都清楚，我想大概所有人也都清楚：美国不是孟加拉国。

sentences.en: The lived experience of a consumer in really what is, on average, the top 5% of the global income distribution, is not the same as it is for the other 95%, and certainly not for the bottom quartile.
sentences.zh: 一个平均处于全球收入分布前5%的消费者的生活体验，和其余95%的人是不一样的，跟收入最低的四分之一人群相比更是天壤之别。

sentences.en: And so, what does a mobile phone mean? What did a mobile phone mean in Bangladesh?
sentences.zh: 那么，一部手机究竟意味着什么？它在孟加拉国又意味着什么？

sentences.en: Actually, Iqbal's brother started the dominant provider of mobile financial services in Bangladesh, so they're a brother pair that have brought not just communications, but banking.
sentences.zh: 其实，伊克巴尔的哥哥创办了孟加拉国占主导地位的移动金融服务公司，所以这对兄弟带来的不仅是通信，还有银行业务。

sentences.en: So, what's the point there? The point is that the phone is not just being able to talk to people.
sentences.zh: 那么这说明了什么？说明手机的意义不只是能跟人说上话。

sentences.en: It's not just being able to make deals, and to understand what prices are, and understand market conditions, and save yourself a day's travel--as occurred with Iqbal in the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 也不只是能谈成生意，了解价格行情，掌握市场状况，省下一整天的奔波——就像伊克巴尔在上世纪七十年代亲身经历过的那样。

sentences.en: One of the reasons that he saw that his favorite phrase, 'Connectivity is productivity.' And, he recalled an episode where he walked half a day to buy some needed medications for one of his siblings, only to find that the pharmacy was closed.
sentences.zh: 这也是他悟出那句他最喜欢的话——“连接就是生产力”——的原因之一。他回忆起一件事：有一次他走了大半天的路，就为了给一个兄弟姐妹买急需的药，结果到了才发现药店关门了。

sentences.en: And then walked home. Now, he's a kid; what's his time worth?
sentences.zh: 然后又走路回家。当时他还是个孩子，他的时间又值多少钱呢？

sentences.en: Not much. But, it's a day of time that you would save--literally a day walking back and forth--that you would save just by a phone call.
sentences.zh: 不值多少钱。但那是白白浪费的一整天时间——实实在在走来走去的一整天——而这一天，本可以靠一通电话就省下来。

sentences.en: And that experience was reinforced over and over again: that connectivity is productivity.
sentences.zh: 这样的经历一次又一次地印证着同一个道理：连接就是生产力。

sentences.en: So, just simply the fact of telecommunication service can be just an incredible time saver, and saving time is saving money.
sentences.zh: 所以，仅仅是有电信服务这件事本身，就能极大地节省时间，而节省时间就是节省金钱。

sentences.en: Saving time is increased productivity. And, beyond that--that's what I get to in later chapters of the book, I only get to mobile financial services--but, the phone has been the delivery mechanism for an array of essential services that simply were not accessible--that did not exist--to the rural poor before mobile phones, just as telecommunication services did not exist.
sentences.zh: 节省时间就是提高生产力。除此之外——这是我在书的后面章节才谈到的，我在书里才写到移动金融服务——手机还是一系列基本服务的传递渠道，而在手机出现之前，这些服务对农村穷人来说根本触及不到，甚至根本不存在，就像电信服务本身也不存在一样。

sentences.en: Landlines never came close to reaching the majority of the world's population.
sentences.zh: 固定电话从来都没能真正覆盖到世界上大多数人口。

sentences.en: And so, it is because we have this abundance of services, abundance of options, abundance of infrastructure, this accumulation of a century of depth of investment in our environment, that the mobile phone seems superfluous.
sentences.zh: 正因为我们拥有丰富的服务、丰富的选择、丰富的基础设施——这一切都是一个世纪以来深厚投资在我们周遭环境中的积累——手机才会显得可有可无。

sentences.en: But it is anything but superfluous to the majority of people on this planet.
sentences.zh: 但对这个星球上大多数人来说，手机绝非可有可无。

sentences.en: And the book is about--in some sense--it's nominally about the mobile phone, but it's also really about the role of entrepreneurship in our lives and in growth.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这本书名义上讲的是手机，但实际上讲的是企业家精神在我们生活和经济增长中所扮演的角色。

sentences.en: So, part of the book traces the rather unknown story, or not well-known story, of how the mobile phone came to be.
sentences.zh: 所以，书里有一部分追溯了手机诞生这段鲜为人知、或者说并不广为人知的历史。

sentences.en: And, you asked the question: Who is responsible for the mobile revolution?
sentences.zh: 而你提出的问题是：移动革命究竟是谁的功劳？

sentences.en: And that's not an easy question to answer.
sentences.zh: 这个问题并不好回答。

sentences.en: But, talk about why that is and, to the extent it is answerable, who is responsible for it.
sentences.zh: 但请谈谈为什么难以回答，以及在多大程度上能够回答——究竟是谁的功劳。

sentences.en: Well, that is not an easy question to answer, and that's really the question I sought to answer in this book.
sentences.zh: 没错，这确实不是个容易回答的问题，而这也正是我在这本书里想要回答的问题。

sentences.en: So, who is responsible?
sentences.zh: 那么，到底是谁的功劳呢？

sentences.en: Entrepreneurs are responsible, inventors are responsible, farsighted government bureaucrats allocating budgets to unlikely projects are responsible, consumers who are willing to try something, adapt to something, are responsible.
sentences.zh: 是企业家的功劳，是发明家的功劳，是那些有远见、愿意把预算投向看似不靠谱项目的政府官员的功劳，也是那些愿意尝试新事物、愿意去适应新事物的消费者的功劳。

sentences.en: And, really, the list goes on. My good friend and somebody who has been an inspiration in my work for 30 years now, Sid Winter wrote an article two decades ago in which he really explored this question of: Who is responsible for a radical technological discontinuity?
sentences.zh: 说实话，这份名单还可以一直列下去。我的好朋友、也是三十年来一直启发我工作的西德·温特，在二十年前写过一篇文章，深入探讨了这个问题：一场彻底的技术断层式变革，究竟是谁的功劳？

sentences.en: And, he used the mobile phones as his example.
sentences.zh: 他当时举的例子就是手机。

sentences.en: I didn't even know that when I started the book, and I came across it.
sentences.zh: 我动笔写这本书的时候其实并不知道这篇文章，是后来偶然发现的。

sentences.en: And so I quote him and cite him at length in the book on exactly this case.
sentences.zh: 所以我在书里就这个案例大段地引用了他的话。

sentences.en: But, so, we've talked about Iqbal, and really, that's later in the story--the market pioneers who did what you might say, 'oh, the last-mile delivery.' But it's not just 'last-mile.' It's to the majority of people worldwide.
sentences.zh: 不过，我们刚才谈到的伊克巴尔，其实是故事比较靠后的部分——他是市场开拓者，你可能会说，这不过是“最后一公里”的事。但这不只是“最后一公里”，而是要覆盖全世界大多数人。

sentences.en: It's not a trivial thing to bring a frontier technology to most people, and that has not been done for many technologies.
sentences.zh: 把一项前沿技术带给大多数人，绝不是件小事，很多技术其实都没能做到这一点。

sentences.en: So, that's where we began. We began with those, what you might say, last-mile pioneers.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们就是从这里开始讲起的。我们从那些可以说是“最后一公里”的开拓者讲起。

sentences.en: But then, you trace it back; then there had to be the initial mobile phone companies in the United States, and those faced a lot of obstacles.
sentences.zh: 但再往前追溯，就必然要提到美国最早的那批手机公司，它们也面临过重重阻碍。

sentences.en: There had to be the inventors. So, you have the Marty Cooper.
sentences.zh: 也必然要有发明家。所以就有了马蒂·库珀。

sentences.en: I tell the story of Marty Cooper at Motorola.
sentences.zh: 我讲述了马蒂·库珀在摩托罗拉的故事。

sentences.en: Which was hardly an upstart, but it really was the challenger to Ma Bell at the time and not the obvious candidate for having developed the first mobile handset.
sentences.zh: 摩托罗拉可算不上什么初出茅庐的新贵，但在当时它确实是挑战“贝尔妈妈”（美国电话电报公司）的角色，而且并不是研发出第一部移动手机的明显人选。

sentences.en: And, Marty Cooper's story is tremendous.
sentences.zh: 马蒂·库珀的故事非常精彩。

sentences.en: Marty is still alive--the guy who made the first call on a mobile handset.
sentences.zh: 马蒂现在还健在——他就是用移动手机打出第一通电话的那个人。

sentences.en: Actually, Iqbal and I did an event with him on the day of the anniversary--50th anniversary--of the first call placed on a mobile handset.
sentences.zh: 其实，在第一通移动电话拨打成功的五十周年纪念日那天，我和伊克巴尔还跟他一起做过一场活动。

sentences.en: So, there's Marty Cooper's story and the whole story of how Motorola developed the first mobile handset.
sentences.zh: 所以书里既有马蒂·库珀的故事，也有摩托罗拉研发出第一部移动手机的整个历程。

sentences.en: And then, you go back again to AT&T, Bell Labs, and this notion that Bell Labs was possibly the greatest single institution responsible for invention in human history.
sentences.zh: 然后再往前追溯，就会回到AT&T、贝尔实验室，以及这样一种说法——贝尔实验室可能是人类历史上单个最伟大的发明机构。

sentences.en: It's a claim that one can credibly make.
sentences.zh: 这是一种站得住脚的说法。

sentences.en: And, mobile telephony is just one technology that really originated across multiple dimensions, not just the transistor, but the network and extension.
sentences.zh: 而移动通信其实只是众多维度共同孕育出的一项技术之一，不只是晶体管，还包括网络和延伸应用。

sentences.en: And, then, of course, we go back to--where did the name Bell come from?
sentences.zh: 当然，接着我们还要追溯——“贝尔”这个名字到底是从哪儿来的？

sentences.en: Alexander Bell. Alexander Graham Bell. So, that's actually where the book begins, is at the Centennial Exposition in Philadelphia, 1876, America's first World's Fair, where Alexander Graham Bell debuted the telephone.
sentences.zh: 亚历山大·贝尔。亚历山大·格拉汉姆·贝尔。所以这本书其实就是从这里开始讲起的：1876年费城百年博览会——美国第一届世界博览会——亚历山大·格拉汉姆·贝尔在那里首次展示了电话。

sentences.en: So, you know, I was thinking when we were talking: 'What an interesting idea that the mobile phone would be transformative.' Well, the landline phone could have been equally transformative, but you'd have to be able to take it with you.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，我们聊着聊着我就在想：“手机会带来变革，这个想法真有意思。”其实固定电话本可以带来同样的变革，只不过前提是你能把它随身带走。

sentences.en: So, the shortcoming of the landline phone is that it's landline--it's in your house, and it stays there.
sentences.zh: 所以固定电话的缺陷就在于它是“固定”的——它待在你家里，也只能待在那儿。

sentences.en: So if you're not in your house, it doesn't help you be more productive or happy or anything else.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你不在家，它就没法帮你提高生产力、变得更快乐，或是带来其他任何好处。

sentences.en: And, it just struck me--you know, when you made that list, one name you left off--two names you left off--which I want to mention, are Claude Shannon and Steve Jobs.
sentences.zh: 我突然想到——你刚才列名单的时候，漏掉了一个名字——其实是两个名字——我想提一下，就是克劳德·香农和史蒂夫·乔布斯。

sentences.en: So, Steve Jobs had this idea that, as you say, we're not as happy about it maybe as we once were, that we have a computer in our pocket at all times.
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫·乔布斯有这样一个理念，就像你说的，也许我们现在不像当初那么欣喜了，那就是：我们口袋里随时都揣着一台电脑。

sentences.en: But what an extraordinary visionary. And, if it was just a phone--if it was all it was was a way to talk to other people--it would be nice and it would be good.
sentences.zh: 但这真是个了不起的远见者。如果它只是一部电话——如果它的全部作用就是让人们能互相通话——那也挺好，挺不错的。

sentences.en: But the productivity--to turn it into a bank, as you point out, it's more than a cow, it's a bank, and many, many, many other things that make people more productive--took a different kind of vision that he brought.
sentences.zh: 但要说到生产力——就像你指出的，要把它变成一家银行，它不只是一头牛，它是一家银行，还是许许多多能提高人们生产力的其他东西——这需要一种不同的远见，而这正是他所带来的。

sentences.en: Claude Shannon laid the intellectual foundations for much of the digital revolution.
sentences.zh: 克劳德·香农为数字革命的大部分理论奠定了基础。

sentences.en: And, although Anthropic, as far as I understand, it does not say that Claude is named after Claude Shannon, he presumably is the namesake of their LLM.So, here's a question I want to ask, having introduced with that.
sentences.zh: 而且，尽管据我所知，Anthropic官方并没有说“Claude”这个名字是以克劳德·香农命名的，但他大概率就是他们那款大语言模型名字的来源。好了，这就引出了我接下来想问的一个问题。

sentences.en: When I was a little boy in the, say, late 1950s, early 1960s, I loved books about explorers.
sentences.zh: 我小时候，大概是上世纪五十年代末、六十年代初，特别喜欢读关于探险家的书。

sentences.en: They were very popular for adults to give books to children about--exploration--Vasco da Gama, Balboa, Drake, Scott, Columbus, you name it.
sentences.zh: 当时大人特别流行送孩子这类关于探险的书——瓦斯科·达伽马、巴尔沃亚、德雷克、斯科特、哥伦布，随便你说哪个都行。

sentences.en: What could be better, right?-- Yeah. Ocean voyages and dangerous missions and so on.
sentences.zh: 还有什么比这更棒的呢，对吧？是啊，远洋航行、危险任务之类的。

sentences.en: And, we learned that later sometimes they had a dark side that we didn't know much about.
sentences.zh: 后来我们才知道，这些人有时候还有我们当年并不了解的阴暗一面。

sentences.en: We weren't told all that when we were seven years old--maybe for the best, maybe not.
sentences.zh: 我们七岁的时候，这些事没人跟我们讲——也许这样更好，也许不是。

sentences.en: No, not back then. No. I'm not saying anything about that.
sentences.zh: 是啊，那时候没人说。不，这个我不予置评。

sentences.en: But, here's the question. They were figures of romance.
sentences.zh: 但问题来了。他们是充满传奇色彩的人物。

sentences.en: Why is it that the intellectual explorers of the 20th century are so obscure?
sentences.zh: 为什么20世纪那些思想领域的探险家却如此默默无闻？

sentences.en: Why is Claude Shannon only a household name to people in the most, more arcane parts of the digital intellectual landscape?
sentences.zh: 为什么克劳德·香农只在数字思想版图里最冷僻的那一小撮圈子里才算得上家喻户晓？

sentences.en: D.H. Ring, a name you mentioned, who envisioned cell phone service.
sentences.zh: 你提到的D.H.林，正是他构想出了蜂窝电话服务。

sentences.en: Yeah, known to absolutely nobody. Almost no one.
sentences.zh: 是啊，几乎没人知道他。几乎无人知晓。

sentences.en: Somebody named Jett, J-E-T-T, you mentioned.
sentences.zh: 你还提到过一个叫杰特的人，J-E-T-T。

sentences.en: Why aren't these people honored and celebrated and used to inspire young people the way physical explorers were?
sentences.zh: 为什么这些人没有像那些实地探险家一样，被人尊崇、被人传颂，被用来激励年轻人呢？

sentences.en: In many ways, they're as, if not more, transformative of our daily lives.
sentences.zh: 从很多方面来说，他们对我们日常生活的改变程度，即便不比那些探险家更大，也至少不相上下。

sentences.en: Any thoughts on that?
sentences.zh: 你对此有什么看法？

sentences.en: Well, there's so much in that question, Russ, I don't even know where to get started.
sentences.zh: 呃，罗斯，这个问题里包含的东西太多了，我都不知道该从哪儿说起。

sentences.en: I mean, you've picked out obviously two very significant names that I did not reference, and just to the point of how many contributors there really were to the mobile revolution.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你挑出的这两个名字显然都非常重要，我在书里并没有提到，这也恰好说明了移动革命背后到底有多少贡献者。

sentences.en: But, let me-- You reference them in the book.
sentences.zh: 但让我——你在书里其实提到过他们。

sentences.en: No, no. -- You didn't mention in that little-- of course, just now.
sentences.zh: 不不。——你刚才那段介绍里没提到——是啊，刚才那段。

sentences.en: Yeah. No, of course. I mean, there's a lot about Claude Shannon, something about Steve Jobs.
sentences.zh: 对。不，当然提到了。我是说，书里关于克劳德·香农写了不少，关于史蒂夫·乔布斯也有一些内容。

sentences.en: So, I want to start by directly answering your question, which is that: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 那我先直接回答你的问题：我不知道。

sentences.en: One of the phrases I developed kind of for the marketing material in this book--I think it's in the introduction someplace--is: 'We too often confuse high net worth with net impact.' And, we're in a culture where we do celebrate entrepreneurs, and these entrepreneurs these days, at least from my vantage point, from how I see things, now have a little bit of a complicated public persona.
sentences.zh: 我为这本书的宣传材料想出过一句话——我记得写在引言的某个地方——“我们太常把高净值和高影响力混为一谈。”我们所处的文化确实推崇企业家，但如今这些企业家——至少从我的角度、我看待事物的方式来说——公众形象已经变得有点复杂了。

sentences.en: When we think about an Elon Musk or a Mark Zuckerberg or so forth and so on.
sentences.zh: 比如说我们想到埃隆·马斯克或马克·扎克伯格之类的人物时就是这样。

sentences.en: So, a decade ago, it was a little simpler.
sentences.zh: 十年前，情况要简单一些。

sentences.en: I remember 15 years ago when Silicon Valley seemed a pretty nice place everyone was excited about.
sentences.zh: 我记得十五年前，硅谷看起来还是个挺不错的地方，大家都对它充满期待。

sentences.en: But these sort of tech titans, as we're thinking about them--there's a tendency, and it is a very flawed and mistaken tendency, a deeply flawed and mistaken tendency, to identify entrepreneurship with those few people--these few very wealthy, Silicon-Valley-situated success stories.
sentences.zh: 但当我们想到这些所谓的科技巨头时——存在一种倾向，而这是一种非常有缺陷、非常错误的倾向，一种根深蒂固的谬误——那就是把企业家精神等同于这少数几个人，等同于这几个身处硅谷、家财万贯的成功故事。

sentences.en: That is not entrepreneurship. It has never been entrepreneurship.
sentences.zh: 那根本不是企业家精神。从来都不是。

sentences.en: It will never be entrepreneurship. It is a very small fraction of what the entrepreneurial process is.
sentences.zh: 以后也永远不会是。那只是整个创业过程中极小极小的一部分。

sentences.en: Strive Masiyiwa and Iqbal Quadir also are not representative.
sentences.zh: 斯特赖夫·马西尤瓦和伊克巴尔·夸德尔其实也不具有代表性。

sentences.en: And, as we know, most entrepreneurship is a single proprietor: It's anybody who takes initiative to build something, create something in the world.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，大多数创业其实是个体经营：只要是主动去建立点什么、创造点什么的人，都算。

sentences.en: So, it's a huge phenomenon, it's a global phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个规模巨大的现象，一个全球性的现象。

sentences.en: I think it's a very significant phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常重要的现象。

sentences.en: But, why do we not celebrate these stories?
sentences.zh: 但为什么我们不去歌颂这些故事呢？

sentences.en: Now, you went beyond entrepreneurship. You talked about E.K.
sentences.zh: 你刚才其实还超出了企业家精神的范畴，提到了E.K.

sentences.en: Jett, who was a government bureaucrat, but who wrote an article for the Saturday Evening Post that was really about the future of mobile telephony, and he wrote it in July 1945.
sentences.zh: 杰特，他是一名政府官员，却为《星期六晚邮报》写过一篇文章，谈的正是移动通信的未来，写作时间是1945年7月。

sentences.en: And, so, it was the same month that Vannevar Bush wrote, As We May Think, talking basically about the Internet.
sentences.zh: 而恰好就在同一个月，范内瓦·布什写下了《诚如所思》，谈的基本上就是互联网的雏形。

sentences.en: So, these two visionaries saw the mobile phone and the Internet at the same time.
sentences.zh: 所以，这两位远见者几乎在同一时间就预见到了手机和互联网。

sentences.en: Now, Vannevar Bush is known-- A little bit-- more than E.K.
sentences.zh: 现在，范内瓦·布什多少还算有点知名度——是有一点——比E.K.

sentences.en: Jett, but so it wasn't just entrepreneurs you talked about.
sentences.zh: 杰特要知名一些，所以你说的可不只是企业家。

sentences.en: And then, Claude Shannon. I mean, if anybody deserves to be a household name in the United States and anywhere else, it's Claude Shannon.
sentences.zh: 然后是克劳德·香农。我是说，如果说有谁配得上在美国乃至全世界都家喻户晓，那非克劳德·香农莫属。

sentences.en: What an incredible figure. What a remarkable individual.
sentences.zh: 多么了不起的人物，多么杰出的一个人。

sentences.en: And, to be able to contribute to adding to that --I mean, of course people do write about Claude Shannon, he is remembered, but, so I don't know the answer to that.
sentences.zh: 能为让他更广为人知出一份力——我是说，当然确实有人写过克劳德·香农，人们也记得他，但我确实不知道这个问题的答案。

sentences.en: I don't know the answer to that. But that's certainly one of the reasons I wrote this book.
sentences.zh: 我不知道答案。但这肯定是我写这本书的原因之一。

sentences.en: Now, if I could just go on one more moment-- Sure-- about Steve Jobs.
sentences.zh: 现在，容我再多说一会儿——当然可以——关于史蒂夫·乔布斯的事。

sentences.en: So, one of the aspects of this story, when we think about--there's a lot of the book, about first third--focuses on Iqbal Quadir's story.
sentences.zh: 这个故事有一个方面——这本书大概前三分之一的篇幅——都聚焦在伊克巴尔·夸德尔的故事上。

sentences.en: And so, why so much about Iqbal? And then, Strive.
sentences.zh: 那为什么要花这么多笔墨写伊克巴尔？然后是斯特赖夫。

sentences.en: And I think they do merit that. So, Iqbal started working on what was Gonophone and then became Grameenphone in 1993--and we already talked about where Bangladesh was at that time.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们确实值得这样的分量。伊克巴尔在1993年开始筹办最初叫Gonophone、后来改名为Grameenphone的公司——当时孟加拉国的情况我们前面已经聊过了。

sentences.en: Iqbal exited Grameenphone. He sold his position in Grameenphone at the same time that Apple was beginning to think about the iPhone.
sentences.zh: 伊克巴尔后来退出了Grameenphone。他卖掉自己在Grameenphone的股份的时候，正好是苹果公司开始构思iPhone的时候。

sentences.en: So, that gives you a sense of how early Iqbal was.
sentences.zh: 这也让你体会到伊克巴尔的起步有多早。

sentences.en: It was certainly not the iPhone that influenced Grameenphone.
sentences.zh: 可以肯定的是，绝不是iPhone影响了Grameenphone。

sentences.en: Grameenphone was in a previous generation.
sentences.zh: Grameenphone属于上一代产品。

sentences.en: Nonetheless, I'm not saying that Steve Jobs doesn't merit his reputation as really one of the great consumer tech visionaries of the last century.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，我并不是说史蒂夫·乔布斯配不上他作为上个世纪伟大消费科技远见者之一的声誉。

sentences.en: And then, Shannon--we could just go on; that could be an entire different podcast around Shannon--but Shannon is a foundational figure in not just mobile telephony, but computing and communications, generally speaking.
sentences.zh: 再说到香农——这个话题可以一直聊下去，围绕香农都能单独做一整期播客了——但总的来说，香农不仅是移动通信领域的奠基性人物，也是计算和通信领域的奠基性人物。

sentences.en: And, somebody to which we owe--whether we want to blame him or thank him--but a lot of the world we exist in was at least significantly advanced or would not exist without Claude Shannon.
sentences.zh: 不管我们是想责怪他还是感谢他，我们都欠他一份人情——我们所处的这个世界，很大一部分，如果没有克劳德·香农，要么进展会大大放缓，要么根本就不会存在。

sentences.en: Yeah, we're all living in Claude's world.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我们都生活在克劳德的世界里。

sentences.en: I think that's what it comes down to. Of course, my other thought--I asked the question; I didn't think about an answer.
sentences.zh: 我想归根结底就是这样。当然，我还有个想法——我提出了这个问题，但其实没想好答案。

sentences.en: I guess the other part of it is that what Claude Shannon understood about the world is harder to convey to a seven-year-old than Balboa.
sentences.zh: 我猜另一个原因是，克劳德·香农对世界的理解，比起巴尔沃亚的故事，要讲给一个七岁孩子听可就难多了。

sentences.en: So, that's definitely part of it. But, I think you're right: I think a lot of it is the money.
sentences.zh: 这肯定是原因之一。不过我觉得你说得对：很大程度上是钱的问题。

sentences.en: For the great explorers, the glamour of risk and discovery, at least for European eyes.
sentences.zh: 对于那些伟大的探险家来说，至少在欧洲人眼中，魅力在于冒险和发现本身。

sentences.en: But for the Internet, the glamour is the money.
sentences.zh: 但对于互联网来说，魅力就是金钱。

sentences.en: And that's a shame. But as you say, that's another story.
sentences.zh: 这真是件憾事。不过就像你说的，那是另一个话题了。

sentences.en: Let's talk a little bit about Adam Smith, who plays a role in this book.
sentences.zh: 我们来聊聊亚当·斯密吧，他在这本书里也扮演了一个角色。

sentences.en: Yes. A person about whom you've done some thinking.
sentences.zh: 没错。一个你对其思想有过一番研究的人物。

sentences.en: Yeah, a little bit. you have some understanding--just a little bit, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，算是有一点吧。你也有些了解——就一点点，是的。

sentences.en: A little bit. I don't pretend I'm an expert on Adam Smith, but I do find him fascinating.
sentences.zh: 就一点点。我不敢说自己是亚当·斯密方面的专家，但我确实觉得他很迷人。

sentences.en: But, Iqbal Quadir, this person who really laid the groundwork for Bangladesh's access to the mobile phone, was very influenced by Smith.
sentences.zh: 而伊克巴尔·夸德尔——这位真正为孟加拉国接入移动通信打下基础的人——深受斯密的影响。

sentences.en: Talk about in what way, and what role Smith played, say, relative to the academic side of development economics.
sentences.zh: 说说具体是哪方面受到影响，以及相对于发展经济学的学术研究，斯密又扮演了怎样的角色。

sentences.en: In some sense--you know, we say Adam Smith was the first economist--you could argue he's the first psychologist.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说——我们常说亚当·斯密是第一位经济学家——你也可以说他是第一位心理学家。

sentences.en: I like to say he was the first social scientist.
sentences.zh: 我更愿意说，他是第一位社会科学家。

sentences.en: He sat in his armchair and he tried to figure out how the world worked, right?
sentences.zh: 他坐在扶手椅上，试图弄明白这个世界是怎么运转的，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah. Yeah. But, academics--they do that, but they also worry about getting papers published and their CV.
sentences.zh: 对，对。但如今的学者们——他们也做这些事，但同时还得操心论文能不能发表、简历好不好看。

sentences.en: But, Smith was just trying to figure stuff out.
sentences.zh: 而斯密纯粹只是想把事情弄明白。

sentences.en: And, why is that still useful today? And, how does that, at least in your mind or Iqbal's, contrast with the academic literature?
sentences.zh: 为什么这种做法在今天依然有用？至少在你或者伊克巴尔看来，这和学术文献相比又有何不同？

sentences.en: So, there are a lot of different types of entrepreneurs, and I'm not at all going to make the claim that Iqbal, who as I indicate and as I describe in the book, I know well, is typical.
sentences.zh: 企业家有很多不同的类型，而我完全不打算说伊克巴尔——正如我在书里提到并描述的那样，我对他非常了解——是个典型代表。

sentences.en: I don't necessarily think he's atypical, either, in the specific regard that I'm about to mention, which is that: Above all, he's an economic theorist.
sentences.zh: 但我也不认为，就我接下来要说的这个特定方面而言，他是非典型的：首先，他其实是一位经济理论家。

sentences.en: He is somebody who, from the very beginning, was interested in ideas, interested in history, and focused on the practical application of what he learned from studying Smith and Hayek and works of history that he engaged with very deeply in his 20s and 30s.
sentences.zh: 他从一开始就对思想、对历史充满兴趣，并且专注于把从研读斯密、哈耶克以及他在二三十岁时深入钻研的各种历史著作中学到的东西，付诸实际应用。

sentences.en: And, that didn't just inform, but really formed his notion for Grameenphone.
sentences.zh: 而这不仅仅是给他一些启发，更是真正塑造了他对Grameenphone的构想。

sentences.en: So, Grameenphone is a expression of an understanding derived from theory, and a successful one.
sentences.zh: 所以，Grameenphone其实是一种源自理论理解的具体表达，而且是一次成功的表达。

sentences.en: And among the theorists who was most influential in this was Adam Smith.
sentences.zh: 而在这些理论家当中，对他影响最深的正是亚当·斯密。

sentences.en: So, now let's sort of contextualize Adam Smith.
sentences.zh: 那我们不妨把亚当·斯密放到具体的语境里来看看。

sentences.en: I certainly do not claim to be an expert on Adam Smith, but any of us who is in the field of economics, we're all fans or influenced one way or the other.
sentences.zh: 我当然不敢说自己是亚当·斯密方面的专家，但凡是从事经济学的人，多少都是他的拥趸，或多或少都受过他的影响。

sentences.en: My favorite book about Smith is actually Albert Hirschman's The Passions and the Interests, which is barely about Smith at all, but is about the couple of centuries of economic thinking that led up to Smith.
sentences.zh: 我个人最喜欢的一本关于斯密的书，其实是阿尔伯特·赫希曼的《激情与利益》，这本书几乎没怎么正面写斯密，讲的是在斯密之前那几个世纪的经济思想演变。

sentences.en: And, for anybody who has not read that book, I would say that is one of my top five favorite books in economics and just is full of really great insights that I believe are actually directly relevant to A Phone Is a Cow.
sentences.zh: 如果谁还没读过这本书，我要说，这是我最喜欢的五本经济学著作之一，里面充满了精彩的洞见，我相信这些洞见其实和《手机就是一头牛》有着直接的关联。

sentences.en: And, so, one of the beautiful things about, I think, the way that Iqbal was influenced by Smith, is it makes us rethink history as we understand it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，伊克巴尔受斯密影响的方式有个美妙之处，就在于它促使我们重新审视我们所理解的历史。

sentences.en: So, just: quick digression. This year we are celebrating the 250th Anniversary of the founding of the United States of America, or at least the Declaration of Independence.
sentences.zh: 稍微岔开一下话题：今年我们正在庆祝美利坚合众国建国250周年，或者至少是《独立宣言》发表250周年。

sentences.en: And so, one of the hallmark events that leading up to the Declaration of Independence was the Boston Tea Party, and that was a reaction to taxation without representation.
sentences.zh: 在《独立宣言》发表之前，有一个标志性事件就是波士顿倾茶事件，那是对“无代表不纳税”这一状况的反抗。

sentences.en: Right? So, the Crown imposed taxes on the colonies, and we did not have a role in that.
sentences.zh: 对吧？英国王室向殖民地征税，而我们在这个过程中毫无发言权。

sentences.en: A question that's not asked, often, is: Why were those taxes imposed to begin with?
sentences.zh: 有个问题却很少有人问：这些税一开始为什么会被征收？

sentences.en: And the reason is: The taxes were imposed to finance Britain's colonization of Bengal.
sentences.zh: 原因是：征收这些税，是为了给英国对孟加拉的殖民统治提供资金。

sentences.en: Which was in some ways the economic center of Asia and a crossroads of the world.
sentences.zh: 而孟加拉在某种程度上，正是当时亚洲的经济中心，也是世界的交通要冲。

sentences.en: Bengal--the textile revolution began in Bengal and actually then migrated to the United Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 孟加拉——纺织业革命最早就发端于孟加拉，后来才转移到了英国。

sentences.en: And so, Bengal was a place of tremendous importance and significance and was Britain's first expansionary colony, the colony of subjugation.
sentences.zh: 所以，孟加拉是一个极为重要、极具意义的地方，它是英国第一块扩张性的殖民地——一块被征服的殖民地。

sentences.en: The United States was a colony of colonization, Bengal was a colony of subjugation.
sentences.zh: 美国是一块“移民型”殖民地，而孟加拉则是一块“征服型”殖民地。

sentences.en: And that required tremendous expenditures to maintain.
sentences.zh: 而维持这样的殖民统治，需要耗费巨额的资金。

sentences.en: And, that's the reason we had the American Revolution, was because we were taxed to finance Bengal.
sentences.zh: 这正是美国独立战争爆发的原因——我们被征税，就是为了给孟加拉的殖民统治买单。

sentences.en: So, there's a complete--we only think about Bangladesh.
sentences.zh: 所以这完全是——我们通常只想到孟加拉国现在的样子。

sentences.en: You know: Concert for Bangladesh and the famine and the revolution and the miserable history of Bangladesh in the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 你知道的：“孟加拉国援助演唱会”、大饥荒、独立战争，还有孟加拉国在上世纪七十年代那段悲惨的历史。

sentences.en: Most people in the United States have not gotten past that idea.
sentences.zh: 大多数美国人的印象都还停留在这个阶段，没能再往前走一步。

sentences.en: That's still where we think about Bangladesh: desperately poor place; Muhammad Yunus, Grameen Bank, all the rest of it, right?
sentences.zh: 我们对孟加拉国的认知还停留在那里：一个极度贫困的地方；穆罕默德·尤努斯、格莱珉银行，诸如此类的印象，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, there's a lot more to the story of Bangladesh and to Bengal.
sentences.zh: 但其实，孟加拉国和孟加拉地区的故事远不止于此。

sentences.en: And Smith saw that. Smith wrote about Bengal as this sort of crown jewel.
sentences.zh: 斯密看到了这一点。斯密笔下的孟加拉，是那种“皇冠上的明珠”式的存在。

sentences.en: And, he also wrote about Bengal as a place whose wealth was derived from its communications network, going back to what we were discussing about earlier, but where, in the case of Bengal, the communications network consisted of rivers and channels and waterways that connected the country as a delta country--it's the delta of the Ganges River.
sentences.zh: 他还写到，孟加拉的财富其实来源于它的通信网络——这又回到我们之前讨论的话题——只不过就孟加拉而言，这个通信网络指的是河流、水道和航道，把这个位于三角洲的国家——也就是恒河三角洲——连接在了一起。

sentences.en: That, they connected the country in an exceptional manner.
sentences.zh: 这些水道以一种非同寻常的方式把整个国家连接了起来。

sentences.en: And that allowed commerce to flow from the coast to the interior.
sentences.zh: 也正因如此，商贸才得以从沿海一路流向内陆。

sentences.en: And so, Smith wrote very eloquently both about Bengal's wealth, and also about its subjugation.
sentences.zh: 所以，斯密既生动地写到了孟加拉的富庶，也写到了它遭受的征服。

sentences.en: So, to see--to discover--as a young Bengali at Wharton in the readings of the writings of Adam Smith, to see Bengal reflected and celebrated was tremendously empowering for Iqbal.
sentences.zh: 所以，作为一名在沃顿商学院求学的年轻孟加拉人，能在亚当·斯密的著作里读到、发现孟加拉的形象被反映出来，甚至被赞颂，这对伊克巴尔来说是极大的鼓舞。

sentences.en: And, from then forward, I think he really reinforced his notion that the misery that he knew of his country was not the totality of the story.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，我认为他更加坚定了一个信念：他所熟知的祖国的苦难，并不是这个故事的全部。

sentences.en: That there was a before and there would be an after.
sentences.zh: 曾经有过“之前”，也终将迎来“之后”。

sentences.en: And he was committed to being part of that after.
sentences.zh: 而他决心要成为那个“之后”的一部分。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's very beautiful. The other part you talk about, which I find very inspiring, is the power of human agency.
sentences.zh: 是啊，这真的很美。你谈到的另一点，我觉得特别鼓舞人心，就是人的能动性的力量。

sentences.en: The ability of people to imagine a future for themselves or for others through products they might bring to the world, and make it happen.
sentences.zh: 人们有能力通过自己可能带给这个世界的产品，为自己或他人构想一个未来，并将其付诸实现。

sentences.en: And of course, it doesn't always happen.
sentences.zh: 当然，这样的事并不总能发生。

sentences.en: When it does happen, it's not always successful.
sentences.zh: 即便发生了，也不总能成功。

sentences.en: But this idea that we have some control over our destiny--which is a very American idea--but it's also a very Smithian idea.
sentences.zh: 但“我们对自己的命运多少握有掌控权”这种理念——这是一种非常美式的理念——同时也是一种非常斯密式的理念。

sentences.en: And it's an unappreciated idea for its novelty, because through most of human history, people thought of themselves as pawns.
sentences.zh: 而这种理念的新颖之处却没有得到应有的重视，因为在人类历史的大部分时间里，人们都把自己看作是棋盘上的棋子。

sentences.en: And of course, in the Marxist viewpoint, you're a pawn of your class: you're oppressed often.
sentences.zh: 当然，在马克思主义的观点里，你是所属阶级的棋子：常常是被压迫的一方。

sentences.en: Most of the world is in that viewpoint. The idea that you have a choice and the ability to make something that isn't there before of yourself, or to do something for other people that's not charity but will actually benefit them--and you--through their purchase of your product.
sentences.zh: 世界上大多数人都持这种观点。而“你拥有选择权和创造能力，能把原本不存在的东西变出来，或者能为别人做点什么——这不是施舍，而是通过他们购买你的产品，真正让他们受益，同时也让你自己受益”这样的想法，就完全不同了。

sentences.en: I never really appreciated, as a Smithian idea, this idea of self-interest in its sense of destiny and molding your future.
sentences.zh: 我以前从没真正意识到，这种把自利与命运感、塑造未来联系在一起的想法，其实是一种斯密式的理念。

sentences.en: Yeah. Well, I mean, Russ, I won't exaggerate things or seem to pander excessively by saying that I wrote this book just with the intent of appearing on EconTalk.
sentences.zh: 是啊。呃，我是说，罗斯，我不想夸大其词，也不想显得过度讨好——但要说我写这本书就是为了能上EconTalk，那倒也不至于。

sentences.en: It's a lot of effort, more than five years, just for this hour--which, by the way, I do enjoy and appreciate.
sentences.zh: 花了这么多心血，五年多的时间，就为了这一个小时——顺便说一句，我确实很享受、也很感激这一个小时。

sentences.en: But, this is one aspect of the book that I really thought you singularly would appreciate, because we don't have that many philosophers in economics.
sentences.zh: 不过，这确实是这本书里我觉得特别对你胃口的一个方面，因为经济学界并没有那么多哲学家。

sentences.en: And, I'm not saying we should. I mean, it's become a very technical discipline.
sentences.zh: 我不是说我们应该有更多哲学家。我是说，经济学已经变成了一门非常技术化的学科。

sentences.en: And, what constitutes a big idea in economics from the standpoint of the history of economic thought is not a very big idea.
sentences.zh: 而从经济思想史的角度来看，如今经济学里所谓的“大理念”，其实算不上什么大理念。

sentences.en: And so--but this is a big idea.
sentences.zh: 但这个——这才算得上是一个真正的大理念。

sentences.en: Predestination and agency, juxtaposed, is a big idea.
sentences.zh: 宿命论与能动性并置在一起，这就是一个大理念。

sentences.en: It's a bigger idea than me, it's a bigger idea than you.
sentences.zh: 这个理念比我要宏大，也比你要宏大。

sentences.en: It is among the biggest ideas that exist that we have.
sentences.zh: 它是我们所拥有的诸多理念中最宏大的那一批之一。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: Choice, free will, or destiny? God's will, or our own agency?
sentences.zh: 选择、自由意志，还是命运？是神的旨意，还是我们自身的能动性？

sentences.en: And so, that's the third level. Right? You talked about--the first level is the mobile phone, and Iqbal and Claude Shannon, and this detailed history--which I just loved getting into.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是第三个层面。对吧？你刚才说到——第一个层面是手机本身，是伊克巴尔和克劳德·香农，是这段详尽的历史——我特别喜欢深入其中。

sentences.en: And to me, that was the fun of the book.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这正是这本书有趣的地方。

sentences.en: Right? And then there's this next level of the history of technology: How do we think about economic development, theories of economic development?
sentences.zh: 对吧？然后是下一个层面，也就是技术史层面：我们该如何看待经济发展、经济发展理论？

sentences.en: And so, there's a kind of like a theory level, but then it occupies.
sentences.zh: 所以，这算是一种理论层面，它占据着自己的位置。

sentences.en: And then, there's this philosophical level.
sentences.zh: 然后，还有这个哲学层面。

sentences.en: So, the closest I get to that is talking about Tolstoy's second epilogue to War and Peace.
sentences.zh: 所以我离这个层面最近的一次，就是谈到了托尔斯泰为《战争与和平》所写的第二篇尾声。

sentences.en: And actually, Tolstoy has a--this is one thing I bookmarked--so, it was a long passage, but at the end of it, Tolstoy writes, "Reason gives expression to the laws of inevitability.
sentences.zh: 事实上，托尔斯泰有一段话——这是我特意标记下来的——是一段很长的文字，但结尾处托尔斯泰写道：“理性表达的是必然性的法则。

sentences.en: Consciousness gives expression to the essence of freedom.
sentences.zh: 意识表达的是自由的本质。”

sentences.en: "And so, he juxtaposes this notion of inevitability--which could be technological inevitability.
sentences.zh: 于是他把这种必然性的观念并置在一起——这种必然性可以是技术上的必然性。

sentences.en: How much does it matter that we had Iqbal Quadir or Strive Masiyiwa?
sentences.zh: 有没有伊克巴尔·夸德尔或斯特赖夫·马西尤瓦这样的人，真的那么重要吗？

sentences.en: Right? Once you had the building blocks of a mobile phone--once you had the value that a mobile phone creates--it was going to get to Bangladesh.
sentences.zh: 对吧？一旦有了手机的基本构成要素——一旦手机能创造的价值已经具备——它迟早会传到孟加拉国。

sentences.en: Does it really matter that one or another person did it?
sentences.zh: 到底是谁去做成这件事，真的那么重要吗？

sentences.en: Do we have any choice at all in our technological future?
sentences.zh: 我们对自己的技术未来，到底有没有一丝选择的余地？

sentences.en: Once something is created in a planet of eight billion people, someone's going to figure it out.
sentences.zh: 在一个拥有八十亿人口的星球上，一旦某样东西具备了被创造出来的条件，总会有人把它琢磨出来。

sentences.en: And, if someone decides not to do something, somebody else will do it.
sentences.zh: 如果有人决定不去做某件事，自然会有别人去做。

sentences.en: Nuclear weapons, whatever it happens to be, these things are all inevitable in some sense, in some way of thinking.
sentences.zh: 核武器也好，其他任何东西也罢，从某种意义上、按某种思路来看，这些事情都是必然会发生的。

sentences.en: Our reason tells us that. Our minds tell us that we really have no way of controlling these forces that are beyond us.
sentences.zh: 我们的理性告诉我们这一点。我们的头脑告诉我们，对于这些超乎我们掌控的力量，我们其实无能为力。

sentences.en: And, the political philosophy of inevitability is Marxism.
sentences.zh: 而“必然性”这一政治哲学，对应的正是马克思主义。

sentences.en: And, it's Marxism, not in a derogatory term.
sentences.zh: 我说马克思主义，并没有贬义。

sentences.en: It's not to say, 'Oh, it's bad Marxism.' It's thoughtful Marxism.
sentences.zh: 我不是说“哦，这是糟糕的马克思主义”。这是经过深思熟虑的马克思主义。

sentences.en: It's thinking about history as, very specifically, class struggle; but beyond that, simply an inevitable force in which human beings play no significant part.
sentences.zh: 它把历史具体地理解为阶级斗争；但除此之外，也把历史看作一股不可避免的力量，在这股力量面前，人类几乎起不到什么重要作用。

sentences.en: And then we have the opposite: the Great Man theory of history.
sentences.zh: 而与之相对的，是“伟人史观”。

sentences.en: Right? And, it could be the Steve Jobs, it could be the Iqbal, it could be the anybody.
sentences.zh: 对吧？可以是史蒂夫·乔布斯，可以是伊克巴尔，可以是任何一个人。

sentences.en: It could be the Mother Teresa. These exceptional people who, without whom, nothing that we see would have occurred.
sentences.zh: 也可以是特蕾莎修女。正是这些非凡的人物，如果没有他们，我们今天所看到的一切都不会发生。

sentences.en: I just said that about Claude Shannon, right?
sentences.zh: 我刚才不就是这么说克劳德·香农的吗？

sentences.en: You said we're all living in Claude's world.
sentences.zh: 你说我们都生活在克劳德的世界里。

sentences.en: And, so, how is this resolved? And, in my view--and I've held this view for a very long time: if there's a single idea that's motivated my intellectual interest for the last 30-plus years--it is the notion that they're both true.
sentences.zh: 那么，这个矛盾要怎么化解呢？在我看来——而且我一直以来都持这种看法：如果说有一个理念在过去三十多年里一直驱动着我的求知兴趣，那就是——这两种说法其实都成立。

sentences.en: It's just not that hard a problem. I mean, it's made out to be a hard problem.
sentences.zh: 这其实并不是一个多难的问题。我是说，是人们把它渲染成了一个难题。

sentences.en: The whole struggle between Socialism and Capitalism is made out to be a very hard problem.
sentences.zh: 社会主义与资本主义之间的整场论战，都被渲染成了一个极为棘手的问题。

sentences.en: Is everything inevitable, or are we these just sort of capitalist, free-will people, Ayn Randian creators: Is it one or the other?
sentences.zh: 到底一切都是必然的，还是说我们其实是那种信奉资本主义、拥有自由意志、像安·兰德笔下那种“创造者”一样的人：非此即彼吗？

sentences.en: It's both, it's just both. And, that's what I loved about Sid's piece.
sentences.zh: 两者兼而有之，就是这么简单。这也正是我喜欢西德那篇文章的地方。

sentences.en: Even though it's just a couple of pages, it's very simple.
sentences.zh: 尽管那篇文章只有短短几页，道理却非常简单明了。

sentences.en: It's both. We have entrepreneurial initiative, we have free will, and we exist in a world in which a lot is predetermined.
sentences.zh: 两者兼有。我们拥有创业主动性，拥有自由意志，同时又生活在一个许多事情早已被注定的世界里。

sentences.en: They simultaneously--they coexist in this sort of magical way.
sentences.zh: 这两者同时——以一种近乎神奇的方式共存着。

sentences.en: At least that's the way I see it. I can't see it any other way.
sentences.zh: 至少我是这么看的。我实在想不出别的理解方式。

sentences.en: And, that's really what I'm intending to say in this book.
sentences.zh: 而这正是我在这本书里真正想表达的东西。

sentences.en: That's what the book is fundamentally about: is to explore this duality of truly exceptional people who have capacities that other people do not have, who have determination that other people do not have, who deserve to be celebrated in just the way you said earlier.
sentences.zh: 这正是本书最根本的主题：探讨这样一种二元性——一方面，是那些真正非凡的人，他们拥有旁人不具备的能力，拥有旁人不具备的意志力，值得像你之前说的那样被歌颂；

sentences.en: We should be telling these stories. And, at the same time, there's this combinatorial progression of change over which we have not that much control, and these things exist simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 我们应该讲述这些故事。而与此同时，又存在着这样一种组合式的渐进变化，我们对它并没有太多掌控力，而这两者是同时存在的。

sentences.en: Yeah. I would just put a little footnote to that.
sentences.zh: 是啊。我想为此补充一个小小的注脚。

sentences.en: It's not so much that we don't have control.
sentences.zh: 与其说我们毫无掌控力，

sentences.en: It's that the sense in which individuals contribute to it is a little more easier to predict.
sentences.zh: 不如说个体在其中所起的作用，其实要更容易预测一些。

sentences.en: The incentives are overwhelming, and they will win out.
sentences.zh: 激励因素的力量太过强大，它们终将胜出。

sentences.en: Those market forces are going to push us to certain outcomes.
sentences.zh: 那些市场力量将把我们推向某些特定的结果。

sentences.en: They will be enacted by individuals making choices.
sentences.zh: 而这些结果会通过个体做出的种种选择去实现。

sentences.en: The speed at which they happen will depend on individuals.
sentences.zh: 而这些结果发生的速度，则取决于个体。

sentences.en: Who they benefit, how they benefit people at certain points.
sentences.zh: 取决于这些结果让谁受益，又在哪些节点上让人们受益。

sentences.en: Exactly. But, the idea of how we should look at our fate and how much of it is up to us: Obviously, it depends on where you live and where you're born, who your parents were, and so on.
sentences.zh: 没错。但关于我们该如何看待自己的命运、其中有多少是我们自己能掌控的——显然，这取决于你生活在哪里、出生在哪里、父母是谁，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But, the idea that Smith saw self-interest--which I think we think of usually as grasping, or as how I come down when I'm faced with a choice, say in a negotiation whether to leave money on the table or not, should I put myself first, and so on--there's such a broader view of that self-interest that you capture that is about our desire to remake the world in our own image, to forge it, to craft it, and your view that that's really what growth is about.
sentences.zh: 但斯密所理解的自利——我们通常把自利理解为贪婪，或者理解为我在面临选择时会怎么做，比如在谈判中要不要把利益留一部分在桌面上，要不要把自己放在第一位，诸如此类——你所捕捉到的这种自利，其实有一个宽广得多的视角，它关乎我们想要按照自己的模样去重塑世界、去锻造它、去打磨它的欲望，而你的看法是，这才是经济增长真正的意义所在。

sentences.en: It's not this inevitable 3% a year most of the time--it's sometimes two and a half--but rather, this extraordinary range of options and endowments that we have of products that already exist and asking, how might we combine some with others to make something that isn't here yet?
sentences.zh: 增长不是那种大多数时候必然维持在3%——偶尔是2.5%——的年增长率，而是我们所拥有的一整套非凡丰富的选项和禀赋——那些已经存在的产品，然后不断追问：我们能不能把其中一些和另一些组合起来，创造出目前尚不存在的东西？

sentences.en: And, some of those things might take a very, very long time to be imagined if an individual didn't come forward with it at a particular time.
sentences.zh: 而其中有些东西，如果没有某个人在特定的时刻挺身而出把它构想出来，可能要等上很久很久才会被人想到。

sentences.en: I appreciate your qualification, and you phrased it better than I did just now.
sentences.zh: 我很欣赏你这个补充说明，而且你刚才表达得比我更贴切。

sentences.en: It's a little bit of a subtle thing to articulate.
sentences.zh: 这确实是个不太容易讲清楚的微妙之处。

sentences.en: And, I was just looking in the book--you know how it is with books, you finish a book and then I'm well into my next book, and then you get the book-- I just read it today, mostly, so it's a little fresher.
sentences.zh: 我刚才还在书里找——你知道写书就是这样，一本书写完，我很快就投入到下一本书里去了，然后回过头翻这本书——我今天大部分内容才刚重读过，所以印象还比较新鲜。

sentences.en: I read it yesterday, and I thought, this is pretty good, I like this book.
sentences.zh: 我昨天读的，当时就想，这本书写得真不错，我挺喜欢的。

sentences.en: But, that's one of the things I love about--this is not my first experience with this--that when you discover a book, you get the physical book and there's just something about the physical book.
sentences.zh: 不过这也是我特别喜欢的一点——这已经不是我第一次有这种体验了——发现一本书、拿到实体书的时候，纸质书本身总有种特别的感觉。

sentences.en: I'm old school--something about a physical book, even your own physical book, that when you read it, it reads differently.
sentences.zh: 我这人比较老派——实体书总有点特别的地方，哪怕是你自己写的实体书，读起来的感觉也会不一样。

sentences.en: So, I have to say, full disclosure: I like the book.
sentences.zh: 所以我得坦白说：我喜欢这本书。

sentences.en: I mean, I feel like it's probably the best thing I've done, such as it is.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我觉得这大概是我做过的最好的一件事了，虽然也就这样吧。

sentences.en: But, so, I did say that by way of, I wanted to find the specific quote.
sentences.zh: 不过，我刚才这么说是想引出——我想找到那段具体的引文。

sentences.en: Yeah, let's find it. There's a nice quote from Smith.
sentences.zh: 好，我们来找找看。斯密有一段很棒的话。

sentences.en: Well, the quote from Smith, it was a very specific quote.
sentences.zh: 嗯，斯密那段引文，是相当具体的一段话。

sentences.en: Yes, here it is. I found it, amazingly. Oh good, because I was looking it up on mine.
sentences.zh: 找到了，就是这段。真是巧了，我找到了。太好了，我这边也正在找呢。

sentences.en: Go ahead. So, this is about agency:The natural effort of every individual to better his own condition, when suffered to exert itself with freedom and security is so powerful a principle that it is alone, and without any assistance, not only capable of carrying on the society to wealth and prosperity, but of surmounting a hundred impertinent obstructions with which the folly of human laws too often incumbers its operations.... [Adam Smith, An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations, B.IV, Ch.5, paragrah 82] Magnificent.
sentences.zh: 你先说。这段讲的是能动性：每个人都在自然地努力改善自身境况，只要这种努力能在自由和安全的条件下自行发挥，就是一种极为强大的原则——单凭它自身，不需要任何外力协助，不仅能带领社会走向财富与繁荣，还能克服人类法律的愚蠢往往强加于其运作之上的种种不当阻碍……（亚当·斯密，《国富论》，第四篇第五章，第82段）太精彩了。

sentences.en: And of course-- Wealth of Nations, Book Four.
sentences.zh: 当然了——《国富论》，第四篇。

sentences.en: I mean, I almost wanted to read it again, it's so beautiful.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我都想再读一遍了，写得太美了。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's pretty great. No, it's pretty great.
sentences.zh: 是啊，写得相当精彩。真的，相当精彩。

sentences.en: And, I think I've read that quote before, but reading it highlighted like that in the book, it grabbed me in a way it hadn't before.
sentences.zh: 我想我以前读过这段话，但在书里看到它被这样特意标注出来，它打动我的方式跟以前不一样了。

sentences.en: But I want to talk about another economist you mention in the book.
sentences.zh: 不过我想聊聊你在书里提到的另一位经济学家。

sentences.en: And, I thought I understood this paper ["Do Real-Output and Real-Wage Measures Capture Reality?
sentences.zh: 我原以为自己已经理解了这篇论文——《实际产出与实际工资的衡量指标真的反映了现实吗？

sentences.en: The History of Lighting Suggests Not," by William Nordhaus--Econlib Ed.], but I learned something I hadn't thought enough about.
sentences.zh: 照明史给出的答案是否定的》，作者是威廉·诺德豪斯，经济学图书馆版——但我从中学到了一些自己以前思考不够深入的东西。

sentences.en: And, it's a simple thing, but you point it out in a way that forces you to think about it.
sentences.zh: 这本身是件很简单的事，但你指出它的方式，会逼着人不得不去认真思考。

sentences.en: And it's, I think again, a very extremely profound idea.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得，这再一次是一个极其深刻的观点。

sentences.en: So, one of the more extraordinary achievements of human beings is to have illumination available at lower and lower cost.
sentences.zh: 人类最了不起的成就之一，就是能以越来越低的成本获得照明。

sentences.en: And, by lower and lower cost, we don't mean to say the monetary price, because that's not the right way to think about it--and it's different currencies in different countries, and it changes over time, and there's inflation.
sentences.zh: 而所谓“越来越低的成本”，我们指的并不是货币价格，因为那样理解并不合适——不同国家用的货币不同，价格会随时间变化，还有通货膨胀的因素。

sentences.en: But the right way to think about it is: How much does a person have to work to be able to, say, read at night, or watch a play, a musical, at night?
sentences.zh: 正确的思考方式应该是：一个人需要工作多久，才能负担得起比如说晚上读书，或者晚上看一场戏剧、一场音乐剧？

sentences.en: And, that's fallen in unimaginably large ways.
sentences.zh: 而这个成本已经以难以想象的幅度下降了。

sentences.en: It's gotten incredibly cheaper for human beings to enjoy light.
sentences.zh: 人类享受光明的代价，已经变得极其低廉。

sentences.en: And, I thought, yeah, that's cool. And, the size of it, the magnitude--what's fun about the paper is he tries to measure it, and it's crude; doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，是啊，这很酷。而且这个变化的规模、幅度——这篇论文有意思的地方在于，他尝试去量化这个变化，虽然方法比较粗糙，但这不重要。

sentences.en: It's the enormous improvement in the human experience.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，这是人类生活体验的巨大改善。

sentences.en: But, your insight, which I thought was incredible--which I missed when I think about that paper--is, it's not just that the candle got brighter and cheaper.
sentences.zh: 但你的洞见——我觉得非常了不起，也是我以前思考这篇论文时忽略掉的——在于：这不仅仅是蜡烛变得更亮、更便宜了。

sentences.en: It's that we sequenced a set of radically different technologies.
sentences.zh: 而是我们经历了一整套截然不同的技术依次更迭。

sentences.en: In one of them, you go and you kill a whale and you take the innards of the whale and use it to create illumination-- To light streets-- Yeah, and that is really different than how my lights are working right now.
sentences.zh: 其中一种方式是，你出海捕鲸，取出鲸鱼的内脏，用它来产生光亮——用来照亮街道——是啊，这跟我现在用的灯的工作原理完全是两码事。

sentences.en: And, it's not just like, 'Oh, it got better and better.' That's not what happened at all.
sentences.zh: 这不是那种“哦，它一点点变得更好了”的简单过程。事实完全不是这样。

sentences.en: It radically changed over time as people thought of new things.
sentences.zh: 随着人们不断想出新点子，照明技术是被彻底颠覆、重塑的。

sentences.en: I think that's really--well, the part that I think about a lot is how hard it is to measure standard of living, and that's because the transformation is so dramatic.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这其实——呃，我经常琢磨的一点是，衡量生活水平有多难，而这正是因为这种转变实在太剧烈了。

sentences.en: It's not just that, 'Oh, the light's a little cheaper, so you have more purchasing power.' Which is central to that paper-- Right.
sentences.zh: 这不只是“哦，灯光便宜了一点，所以你的购买力提高了”这么简单——这确实是那篇论文的核心内容——没错。

sentences.en: So, that part is in there, but the idea that--and there's a quote which is a one-sentence way--I'm not going to get it verbatim; you'll help me if you know it by heart--that captures this insight.
sentences.zh: 所以那部分内容确实包含在论文里，但还有一个想法——有一句引文能用一句话概括这个洞见——我没法一字不差地背出来，如果你记得的话可以帮我补充。

sentences.en: And it's, I think, an incredibly deep insight for business.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得，这对商业来说是一个极其深刻的洞见。

sentences.en: It relates to Clayton Christensen and The Innovator's Dilemma, which you've talked about recently on the program.
sentences.zh: 它和克莱顿·克里斯坦森以及《创新者的窘境》有关，你最近在节目里也谈到过这本书。

sentences.en: It relates to Development Economics. It's the quote from Henry Ford, which is, 'People didn't know they wanted cars.
sentences.zh: 它也和发展经济学有关。这正是亨利·福特那句名言——“人们当初并不知道自己想要的是汽车。

sentences.en: They thought they wanted faster horses.' Right, right.
sentences.zh: 他们以为自己想要的是跑得更快的马。”对，对。

sentences.en: Yeah, right. And, what they really wanted was to move more quickly; but the only way they could think about it was, 'I wonder if we could feed a horse something, he could move his legs quicker, and I could get across town quicker.'The idea of a car is not just like, 'Well, that's a faster horse.' It's not.
sentences.zh: 是啊，没错。他们真正想要的其实是更快地移动；但他们能想到的唯一方式是，“不知道能不能给马喂点什么东西，让它腿脚更快，我就能更快地穿过城镇了。”而汽车这个概念，绝不只是“这不过是一匹更快的马”而已。完全不是。

sentences.en: It's not a horse. But it is a better way to get across town.
sentences.zh: 它根本不是马。但它是一种更好的、能穿越城镇的方式。

sentences.en: And that is the human experience. I'm getting romantic about it because I think it's incredibly profound.
sentences.zh: 这就是人类的生活体验。我说得有点动情，是因为我觉得这一点极其深刻。

sentences.en: Yeah. I mean, I guess a few of us economists who are specialized in the economics of technology and innovation--I guess any subfield probably talks their way into thinking, like, 'This is the only subfield that matters.' And, so, with deference to all the other subfields in economics--and then when you talk about the economics of Production Theory, which is really my technical area--that's, like, 12 people that care about production.
sentences.zh: 是啊。我是说，我猜我们这些专攻技术与创新经济学的经济学家——我猜任何一个细分领域大概都会把自己说服成“这才是唯一重要的细分领域”。所以，在对经济学其他各个细分领域表示敬意的前提下——再说到生产理论经济学，这其实是我的技术专长所在——关心生产理论的，大概也就十来个人吧。

sentences.en: That's a settled problem: nobody is thinking about the production function.
sentences.zh: 那已经是个定局了的问题：没人还在琢磨生产函数。

sentences.en: But to me, that's an interesting thing to think about.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，这是件值得思考的有趣事情。

sentences.en: So, the Nordhaus paper. The Nordhaus paper perfectly encapsulates what we were just discussing about free will versus inevitability.
sentences.zh: 那说回诺德豪斯的这篇论文。它完美地浓缩了我们刚才讨论的“自由意志与必然性”这个话题。

sentences.en: And you also referenced GDP growth. We could talk about diffusion--technological diffusion, S-shape diffusion curves.
sentences.zh: 你还提到了GDP增长。我们还可以聊聊扩散——技术扩散、S型扩散曲线。

sentences.en: Right? And, you look across any technology, there it is: there's the S-shape diffusion curve.
sentences.zh: 对吧？你随便看哪一项技术，都能发现它：那条S型扩散曲线就在那儿。

sentences.en: Everything is so regular and smooth that it's hard to imagine that there's any discontinuity, any insight, any moment of particular significance underlying it.
sentences.zh: 一切都显得如此规律、如此平滑，让人很难想象其背后竟然存在着某种断层、某种洞见、某个格外重要的时刻。

sentences.en: And so, Nordhaus's paper traces out this incredible decrease in the amount of human effort required to illuminate at night.
sentences.zh: 而诺德豪斯的这篇论文，正是追溯了夜间照明所需人力成本的这种惊人下降。

sentences.en: And so, on its surface--and it's a very powerful paper; and one of the things that it goes back to one million B.C.
sentences.zh: 表面上看——这是一篇非常有力的论文——它追溯的时间线甚至一直回溯到公元前一百万年。

sentences.en: You talk about the long view, it's in terms of-- It's a fire, it's a wood fire-- Yeah, a wood fire.
sentences.zh: 你说的这种长时段视角，说的是——是火，是篝火——对，是篝火。

sentences.en: Yeah, fire, going back to fire. So, in terms of the long view, in terms of the work that's been recognized by the Sveriges Riksbank--the Nobel Prize of Economics, so-called--it's kind of unique.
sentences.zh: 是啊，火，追溯到用火的年代。所以，从这种长时段视角来说，从瑞典银行——也就是所谓的诺贝尔经济学奖——所认可的这项研究来说，它算是相当独特的。

sentences.en: But then, and I guess if I was trying to imagine what might have been new in this book about that paper, maybe I would have guessed correctly, which is the discontinuities underlying that.
sentences.zh: 不过，如果要我猜这本书在这篇论文的基础上又带来了什么新东西，我大概能猜对，那就是这种趋势背后隐藏的断层点。

sentences.en: I can't really improve on the way you characterized it.
sentences.zh: 你刚才的概括，我实在没法讲得更好了。

sentences.en: I was pulling up the table, but you remembered off the cuff a lot of the highlights, and I think that the jump from whale oil to electrification is a terrific example.
sentences.zh: 我刚才还在找那张表格，但你已经脱口而出记住了很多要点，我觉得从鲸油照明跃迁到电气化，就是一个绝佳的例子。

sentences.en: And, we can attack the fossil fuels industry, and of course we're very concerned about climate change and all that, but before that, we were burning fellow mammals.
sentences.zh: 我们现在可以抨击化石燃料产业，当然我们也很关注气候变化之类的问题，但在那之前，我们烧的其实是同为哺乳动物的鲸鱼。

sentences.en: And that was worse. So, I think this-- And, burning down forests to stay warm at night-- And burning down forests, exactly-- Much more than to illuminate, but just to stay alive in certain climates.
sentences.zh: 那其实更糟糕。所以我觉得这个——还有为了在夜里取暖而烧毁森林——没错，烧毁森林——这远不只是为了照明，而是在某些气候条件下单纯为了活下去。

sentences.en: Just to stay alive. So, when we think about technological progress, what seems like regress in some sense--there's always these paradoxes of progress.
sentences.zh: 单纯为了活下去。所以，当我们思考技术进步时，有些从某种意义上看似倒退的东西——进步总是伴随着这样的悖论。

sentences.en: We don't see the way in which we have improved across multiple dimensions, not just efficiency dimensions, but also ethical dimensions, as you were just referencing.
sentences.zh: 我们往往看不到自己已经在多个维度上取得了进步——不只是效率维度，正如你刚才提到的，还包括伦理维度。

sentences.en: So, anyway, yes; that is a core point of the book and it's reflected in that paper.
sentences.zh: 总之，是的，这正是这本书的一个核心观点，也体现在那篇论文里。

sentences.en: And, I guess the big idea is that human progress is about new technologies coming into being and becoming widely used, and that's what this book is about.
sentences.zh: 我想，这个大理念就是：人类的进步，关乎新技术的诞生以及它被广泛使用的过程，而这正是这本书要讲的东西。

sentences.en: It's not just technologies coming into being.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是技术的诞生。

sentences.en: It's not just innovation--what Schumpeter talked about as innovation, a successful market demonstration.
sentences.zh: 也不仅仅是创新——熊彼特所说的创新，是指一次成功的市场验证。

sentences.en: The landline was a successful innovation.
sentences.zh: 固定电话就是一次成功的创新。

sentences.en: It reached hundreds of millions of people.
sentences.zh: 它触及了数以亿计的人口。

sentences.en: But it didn't come close to reaching the majority of people worldwide.
sentences.zh: 但它远远没能触及全世界大多数人口。

sentences.en: The mobile phone did. And so, it's a combination of creating new technologies--what Schumpeter talked about--carrying out new combinations.
sentences.zh: 而手机做到了。所以，这其实是新技术创造——也就是熊彼特所说的——与“实现新组合”的结合。

sentences.en: That was his phrase for entrepreneurship, 'Carrying out new combinations.' It's to bring those market innovations to people.
sentences.zh: “实现新组合”正是他用来定义企业家精神的说法。而这也正是要把这些市场层面的创新带到人们身边。

sentences.en: And that's what Iqbal Quadir did, that's what Strive Masiyiwa did.
sentences.zh: 这正是伊克巴尔·夸德尔所做的事，也正是斯特赖夫·马西尤瓦所做的事。

sentences.en: That's really the focal point of this book, although there's a lot of other elements to the mobile revolution.
sentences.zh: 这确实是这本书真正的焦点所在，尽管移动革命还包含许多其他元素。

sentences.en: And, I will maintain--given my areas of interest and expertise, I will maintain that there is no comparably important question in economics.
sentences.zh: 而我要坚持这样一个观点——基于我的兴趣领域和专业背景——我坚持认为，经济学里没有哪个问题能和这个问题的重要性相提并论。

sentences.en: Because, this is the question of human progress.
sentences.zh: 因为，这正是关乎人类进步的问题。

sentences.en: This is the question of human wellbeing over the period of millennia.
sentences.zh: 这是关乎人类在千年尺度上福祉的问题。

sentences.en: Everything else--about resource allocation, about policy, about macro--everything else is a footnote to this larger question of how new things come into being and how they reach most people.
sentences.zh: 其他一切——资源配置、政策、宏观经济——其他所有问题，相对于“新事物如何诞生、如何触及大多数人”这个更宏大的问题来说，都不过是个注脚。

sentences.en: I cannot see it differently than that. Yeah, it's beautifully said.
sentences.zh: 我实在想不出别的看法了。是啊，这话说得真好。

sentences.en: I want to bring Hayek in, and when you said--when you were talking about the diffusion of technology and innovation, or in this case it would probably be invention--that allowed, say, a filament to bring illumination relative to whale blubber-- Right-- I've never thought about this before, I think, but when you frame it earlier--as we've been doing and in terms of inevitability versus agency--if you think about the Nordhaus insight, that the price of illumination has fallen steadily over time: It's an emergent order/invisible hand argument.
sentences.zh: 我想把哈耶克也拉进来——你刚才说到技术与创新的扩散，或者在这个例子里更准确地说是发明的扩散——正是这种扩散让灯丝相对于鲸脂能带来照明——没错——我以前好像从没这么想过，但按你之前的框架来说——就像我们一直在讨论的必然性与能动性之争——如果你想想诺德豪斯的这个洞见，照明的价格随着时间推移持续下降：这其实是一种“自发秩序／看不见的手”式的论证。

sentences.en: It looks like, if you look at it, that someone must have decreed that this should be-- God's will-- God's will.
sentences.zh: 从表面上看，好像一定有谁下令规定了事情就该如此——是神的旨意——是神的旨意。

sentences.en: Or, it's a natural law, which is not--it's a different way of saying that's similarly.
sentences.zh: 或者说，这是一种自然法则——这其实和刚才那种说法本质相似，只是换了个说法。

sentences.en: And it's similar in the sense that the key point here is the inevitability idea.
sentences.zh: 相似之处就在于，这里的关键点都是“必然性”这个概念。

sentences.en: And, your insight that it's both--the predestination-inevitability combined with individual agency--so they're both happening at the same time.
sentences.zh: 而你的洞见是，两者兼而有之——宿命般的必然性和个体的能动性结合在一起——这两者是同时发生的。

sentences.en: What's driving the illumination is that people like to do things in the dark.
sentences.zh: 推动照明进步的动力，是人们不喜欢在黑暗中做事。

sentences.en: So they want light. They want to eat meals at night, they want to go to shows, they want to go to concerts, they want to read, they don't want to be afraid in the winter starting at 4:30 in the afternoon.
sentences.zh: 所以他们需要光。他们想在晚上用餐，想去看演出，想去听音乐会，想读书，不想在冬天下午四点半天一黑就开始感到害怕。

sentences.en: And, that fundamental human urge has allowed thousands of people over human history to better themselves by creating cheaper and better ways to banish darkness.
sentences.zh: 正是这种根本性的人类需求，让人类历史上成千上万的人得以通过发明更便宜、更好的方式来驱散黑暗，从而改善自己的处境。

sentences.en: And, it's both. There is an inevitability, which is driven by the human desire for illumination; but you couldn't have that inevitability without the crazy insights of people to come up with crazy ways of achieving that, which couldn't be predicted until they happened.
sentences.zh: 两者兼有。存在一种由人类对光明的渴望所驱动的必然性；但如果没有那些人想出各种疯狂点子、以疯狂的方式去实现这种渴望，这种必然性根本无从谈起——而这些点子在真正发生之前，是完全无法预测的。

sentences.en: And to say, 'Well, eventually I knew someone would have figured out a cheaper way to do it,' it's easy to say.
sentences.zh: 事后说一句“嗯，我早就知道迟早会有人想出更便宜的办法”，说起来倒是容易。

sentences.en: But it's not gravity. It's not inevitable.
sentences.zh: 但这不是万有引力那样的定律。它并非注定如此。

sentences.en: It requires, at the same time, incentives to be in place for people to profit from that innovation and that invention.
sentences.zh: 它同时还需要有相应的激励机制到位，让人们能够从这种创新和发明中获利。

sentences.en: And, that's really a beautiful thing. We talk about Moore's law, and people would ask the question, 'What kind of a law is it?' I mean, why should it be that we can always expand the capability of chips at a certain rate of computer chips?
sentences.zh: 这真是件很美妙的事。我们谈到摩尔定律，人们会问：“这算是哪门子定律？”我是说，为什么我们总能按照某个固定速率不断扩展计算机芯片的性能呢？

sentences.en: And you have the answer, and I've never heard a better one: Which is this combination.
sentences.zh: 而你给出了答案，我还从没听过比这更好的答案：那就是这种“组合”。

sentences.en: It looks predestined. It's not. You could kill it.
sentences.zh: 它看起来像是命中注定的。其实不是。你完全可能扼杀它。

sentences.en: You could kill it easily with the wrong legislation and the wrong set of regulatory rules.
sentences.zh: 只要立错了法、定错了一套监管规则，就能轻而易举地把它扼杀掉。

sentences.en: But if you keep the incentives there for improvement, people will develop ways to do it, even though you may not know how they will.
sentences.zh: 但只要持续保留改进的激励机制，人们就会想出办法来实现改进，尽管你未必知道他们具体会怎么做。

sentences.en: And, that's the Nordhaus story and it's a Smith-Tolstoy story, if I may be a little bold.
sentences.zh: 这就是诺德豪斯的故事，如果我可以稍微大胆一点说，这也是一个斯密加托尔斯泰式的故事。

sentences.en: Absolutely. And, actually, you went in a direction--and it was part of your question I didn't answer.
sentences.zh: 完全同意。而且实际上，你刚才引到了一个方向——那正是你问题里我还没回答的一部分。

sentences.en: But, it's another way of thinking about not just the core contribution, such as it is, of this book, but actually of my last three books--my only general-audience books going back to 2012.
sentences.zh: 但这也是另一种思考角度，不仅关乎这本书的核心贡献本身——虽然这个贡献也就那样吧——其实还关乎我最近三本书，也就是我从2012年以来唯一面向大众读者的几本著作。

sentences.en: There's sort of a trilogy, and underlying that is this idea inspired by Schumpeter, that entrepreneurship and innovation are the carrying out of new combinations.
sentences.zh: 这算是一个三部曲，而贯穿其中的，是受熊彼特启发的这样一个理念：企业家精神和创新，就是“实现新组合”。

sentences.en: And, this was 1911; and you know, Schumpeter, before we had evolutionary biology--before we understood DNA, before we really understood the fundamentally combinatorial nature of life itself, not to mention technology--he had that insight, that there was something combinatorial about innovation.
sentences.zh: 那是1911年的事；要知道，在演化生物学出现之前——在我们理解DNA之前，在我们真正理解生命本身在根本上具有组合性质之前，更别提技术了——熊彼特就已经有了这样的洞见：创新本质上带有某种组合性质。

sentences.en: Now, the great Marty Weitzman had--whose contributions span so many different fields, almost to Kenneth Arrow, I would say, very close--had a paper called "Hybridizing Growth Theory," which is my favorite paper in the growth literature.
sentences.zh: 伟大的马蒂·魏茨曼——他的贡献横跨众多领域，我甚至要说，几乎可以和肯尼斯·阿罗相提并论——写过一篇论文，叫《杂交增长理论》，那是我在增长理论文献中最喜欢的一篇论文。

sentences.en: And, it also borrows from this notion of innovation being fundamentally combinatorial.
sentences.zh: 这篇论文同样借鉴了“创新在本质上是组合性的”这一理念。

sentences.en: My friend and mentor, Stuart Kauffman, with whom I wrote some early papers, is known for his insight about the 'adjacent possible,' that Steven Johnson then picked up on.
sentences.zh: 我的朋友兼导师斯图尔特·考夫曼——我早年和他一起写过几篇论文——以他关于“临近可能”的洞见而闻名，后来史蒂文·约翰逊也接过了这个概念。

sentences.en: And, the 'adjacent possible' is fundamentally combinatorial.
sentences.zh: 而“临近可能”在本质上就是一种组合性的概念。

sentences.en: When you have a set of Lego pieces and you arrange them in a certain way, then given the configuration that you're holding in your hand, there are certain kind of imminent next steps based on the combinatorial nature of the thing you've created.
sentences.zh: 当你手里有一堆乐高积木，并把它们按某种方式拼搭起来之后，基于你手中已经拼出的这个结构所具有的组合性质，就会存在某些呼之欲出的下一步可能。

sentences.en: That you add one piece, subtract one piece: that there's kind of an imminent next possibility in the combinatorial nature of technology that doesn't exist when we think just in terms of scalars.
sentences.zh: 你添上一块，或者拿走一块：这种技术组合性质中蕴含着一种呼之欲出的下一步可能，而当我们只是单纯用标量思维去思考时，这种可能性是不存在的。

sentences.en: And, so, we lose something fundamental when we reduce just to the number line--that technology isn't reducible in that way: it is fundamentally combinatorial.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们把一切都简化成一条数轴时，我们就丢失了某种根本性的东西——技术无法被这样简化：它在本质上是组合性的。

sentences.en: And so, this idea of the adjacent possible is a way of understanding the combination of this paradox of, how do we have free will and inevitability?
sentences.zh: 所以，“临近可能”这个概念，正是一种理解这个悖论组合的方式：我们究竟是如何同时拥有自由意志和必然性的？

sentences.en: And, the way that the adjacent possible and the combinatorial nature of innovation does that, is that the search space for combinatorial innovation is hyper-exponential.
sentences.zh: 而“临近可能”和创新的组合性质之所以能做到这一点，原因在于组合式创新的搜索空间是超指数级增长的。

sentences.en: It is simply impossible to think about in multiple lifetimes of the universe exhaustively searching everything that God has given us as possibilities.
sentences.zh: 就算花上宇宙好几辈子的时间，也根本不可能穷尽搜索上天赋予我们的所有可能性。

sentences.en: So, we must choose a path. And, this whole notion of path dependency that Brian Arthur--somebody else who has been very influential in my work and my career who I had the opportunity to meet in 1993 at the Santa Fe Institute Summer School along with Steven Kauffman--that this idea of path dependency originates in this combinatorial nature of technology.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们必须选择一条路径。而“路径依赖”这整套理念——布莱恩·阿瑟对我的研究和职业生涯影响也非常深远，我1993年有幸在圣塔菲研究所暑期学校见到他，和斯蒂芬·考夫曼一起——路径依赖这个理念，正是源自技术的这种组合性质。

sentences.en: And it is the way in which, what I call combinatorial foresight--free will operates in long-term economic growth.
sentences.zh: 而这也正是我所说的“组合式远见”——自由意志在长期经济增长中发挥作用的方式。

sentences.en: Someone has to choose something to try. Someone has to try it.
sentences.zh: 总得有人去选择尝试点什么。总得有人真去试一试。

sentences.en: Someone has to test it out. It's what Ricardo Hausmann, Dani Rodrik wrote about, is, economic growth is self-discovery.
sentences.zh: 总得有人去把它验证出来。这正是里卡多·豪斯曼、丹尼·罗德里克所写的观点：经济增长就是一种自我发现的过程。

sentences.en: It's the same phenomenon. It's that somebody has to get out there and be that pioneer, be that Vasco da Gama.
sentences.zh: 这其实是同一种现象。总得有人挺身而出，去当那个开拓者，去当那个瓦斯科·达伽马。

sentences.en: And for every Vasco da Gama, we know there's a bunch of people we never heard of who were sitting at the bottom of the sea.
sentences.zh: 而对于每一个瓦斯科·达伽马，我们都知道，还有一大群我们从未听说过的人，早已葬身海底。

sentences.en: Right? All those people had to do something.
sentences.zh: 对吧？所有这些人都必须去做点什么。

sentences.en: And so, to me, when you see life--and Shannon wrote about life and combinatorics.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，当你观察生命——香农也写过关于生命与组合数学的文章。

sentences.en: I mean there was--Schrödinger wrote about it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，还有——薛定谔也写过这个话题。

sentences.en: It was very much imminent at the same time that the mobile phone was being created.
sentences.zh: 在手机诞生的同一时期，这种想法正呼之欲出。

sentences.en: These are the same set of ideas. They're not different ideas.
sentences.zh: 这些其实是同一套理念。它们并非各自独立的理念。

sentences.en: There's the same set of people and ideas who understood the combinatorial nature of technology and who understood the importance of combinatorics in other areas of creation.
sentences.zh: 正是同一批人、同一套理念，既理解了技术的组合性质，也理解了组合数学在其他创造领域中的重要性。

sentences.en: But I want to put an asterisk or a footnote on that.
sentences.zh: 但我想在这里加个星号，或者说打个注脚。

sentences.en: And, again, I learned this from you in your book.
sentences.zh: 而且，这一点我也是从你的书里学到的。

sentences.en: It's true: you write that if you have 20 Lego pieces in a certain configuration, you have two you can add onto it, it's really different than if you have two Lego pieces and two to add onto it.
sentences.zh: 确实如此：你在书里写道，如果你有20块乐高积木、已经拼成某种结构，还能再添两块上去，这和你只有2块乐高积木、也能再添两块上去，情况完全不同。

sentences.en: Once you have a larger and larger stock that you're endowed with, the possibilities do become exponentially--which barely covers it--larger.
sentences.zh: 一旦你所拥有的存量越来越庞大，可能性确实会呈指数级——用“指数级”都还不足以形容——增长。

sentences.en: But, I like your other point, which comes from the Nordhaus insight--your emphasis of the Nordhaus insight--which is: It's true that there's an inevitability about how I'm going to probably add these two pieces when I have 10 already.
sentences.zh: 但我还喜欢你的另一个观点，它来自诺德豪斯的洞见——你所强调的诺德豪斯洞见——那就是：确实存在一种必然性，当我已经有10块积木时，我大概会怎样添上这两块，这在某种程度上是可以预见的。

sentences.en: But, I might want to break up those 10, start from scratch, and with those 12 pieces, achieve the goal I wanted to achieve in a totally different way.
sentences.zh: 但我也可能想把那10块拆开，从头再来，用这12块积木，以一种完全不同的方式去实现我想要达成的目标。

sentences.en: So, for a while, you're trying to harvest whales more and more effectively.
sentences.zh: 所以，有一段时间，你一直在想办法更高效地捕鲸。

sentences.en: Yes, yes, yeah. And, because of property rights, it gets complicated: That has a certain asymptotic, if not negative, impact after a while.
sentences.zh: 对，对，是啊。而由于产权问题，事情变得复杂起来：一段时间之后，这种做法即便不算是负面影响，也会产生某种趋于极限的效果。

sentences.en: But, you do that for a while because that's the easiest game is to rearrange.
sentences.zh: 但你会这样做一阵子，因为这是最简单的做法——重新排列组合。

sentences.en: Not to rearrange: is to add on, is to combine the model you're given with some new stuff.
sentences.zh: 准确说不是重新排列，而是在原有基础上添加，是把你已有的模型和一些新东西结合起来。

sentences.en: But, the genius who comes along and takes it to another level is the one who says, 'You know, I think I could rearrange all the pieces and create something that hasn't been here before.' It's still just a rearrangement, it's still a combination-- Right, right, right, right-- But, 'I'm going to bring a new way of achieving my goals with this new combination.' And that's the visionary.
sentences.zh: 但真正的天才出现之后，会把这件事提升到另一个层次，他会说：“你知道吗，我觉得我可以把所有这些积木全部重新排列，创造出一种前所未有的东西。”这本质上依然是一种重新排列，依然是一种组合——对，对，对，对——但他会说：“我要用这种新的组合方式，找到一种全新的路径去实现我的目标。”而这，正是有远见的人。

sentences.en: Well, yeah, that's right, that's right. And, I think you probably remember--I believe it was 2005, so roughly 20 years ago--the final discovered paper by Schumpeter, by Joseph Schumpeter, was published.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对，没错，没错。而且我想你大概还记得——我记得是2005年，大约二十年前——熊彼特，也就是约瑟夫·熊彼特，最后一篇被发现的论文出版了。

sentences.en: And, if I recall correctly, it was called Development, and it was one of the last papers that Schumpeter wrote.
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，那篇论文题为《发展》，也是熊彼特生前最后写下的论文之一。

sentences.en: And it was on the question of novelty. And so, here, I've been citing Schumpeter as essentially somebody saying that economically meaningful invention--which is to say innovation, carried out by entrepreneurship--is the carrying out of new combinations.
sentences.zh: 那篇论文探讨的正是“新颖性”这个问题。到目前为止，我一直在引用熊彼特，把他当作一位这样说的学者：具有经济意义的发明——也就是说，由企业家精神所推动实现的创新——就是“实现新组合”。

sentences.en: This was Schumpeter's great vision and insight, and I've just been talking about that.
sentences.zh: 这正是熊彼特那伟大的远见和洞察，我刚才一直在谈的也正是这个。

sentences.en: But, toward the end of his life, he was really struggling with this idea of novelty: that, if that is true, then under what circumstances can we say something is truly new to the world?
sentences.zh: 但到了晚年，他其实一直在苦苦思索“新颖性”这个问题：如果上述说法成立，那么在什么条件下，我们才能说某样东西对这个世界来说是真正全新的？

sentences.en: And the one thing that is in that category in my book, the one element of the mobile phone story that I believe is in that category, is the transistor.
sentences.zh: 而在我的书里，唯一真正属于这个“全新”范畴的东西——我认为在整个手机故事里唯一属于这个范畴的元素——就是晶体管。

sentences.en: The transistor was something that was just imagined and discovered--the properties of semiconductors, the possibility of the transistor.
sentences.zh: 晶体管纯粹是被构想出来、被发现出来的东西——半导体的特性、晶体管的可能性。

sentences.en: And, so, going from the vacuum tube to the transistor was one of these discontinuities.
