sentences.zh: 所以，从真空管过渡到晶体管，正是这样一种断层式的跃迁。

sentences.en: But, the transistor itself was useless. You can't do anything with a transistor, right?-- Yeah.
sentences.zh: 但晶体管本身其实毫无用处。单靠一个晶体管你什么都做不了，对吧？——是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah-- You have to use it for something.
sentences.zh: 是啊——你得找到它的用途才行。

sentences.en: And, it was a decade before, first of all, they figured how to make them at any kind of scale.
sentences.zh: 而且，人们花了整整十年时间，首先才弄明白该怎样批量生产晶体管。

sentences.en: And, second of all, what are you going to use it for?
sentences.zh: 其次才是，你到底要拿它来做什么？

sentences.en: Like, it's going to be useful for everything: we know that.
sentences.zh: 我们都知道，它最终会在几乎所有领域都派上用场。

sentences.en: But it's got to be useful for something before it's useful for everything.
sentences.zh: 但它得先在某一件事上派上用场，才能最终在所有事情上派上用场。

sentences.en: So, the transistor was this incredible new Lego piece.
sentences.zh: 所以，晶体管就是那块令人惊叹的全新乐高积木。

sentences.en: Right? Once you have this Lego piece, then you get to the point of, like: Wait, whoa, whoa.
sentences.zh: 对吧？一旦你有了这块积木，你就会突然意识到：等等，哇，哇。

sentences.en: Everything we're thinking about computation is different.
sentences.zh: 我们对计算的一切认知都不一样了。

sentences.en: Everything we're thinking about ultimately of telephony is different.
sentences.zh: 我们对电信最终的一切认知也都不一样了。

sentences.en: Everything we're thinking about--a refrigerator is different.
sentences.zh: 我们对——就连冰箱的一切认知也都不一样了。

sentences.en: Everything becomes different once we have this thing that becomes the chip, right?
sentences.zh: 一旦有了这个后来演变成芯片的东西，一切都变得不一样了，对吧？

sentences.en: It becomes the chip. So, to me, that's another kind of piece of this, is that once we have enough Lego pieces, almost all of invention--I mean, sorry--almost all of innovation, almost all of entrepreneurship, the overwhelming majority is rearranging new pieces.
sentences.zh: 它演变成了芯片。所以对我来说，这是这件事的另一块拼图：一旦我们拥有了足够多的积木，几乎所有的发明——不好意思，我是说几乎所有的创新、几乎所有的创业活动——绝大多数其实都是在重新排列这些新积木。

sentences.en: And a lot of it is just bringing existing stuff to markets that don't have it anymore.
sentences.zh: 而其中很多不过是把已经存在的东西，带到那些原本还没有它的市场里去。

sentences.en: Iqbal did not invent anything; he barely innovated anything.
sentences.zh: 伊克巴尔并没有发明任何东西，他甚至几乎没有创新什么东西。

sentences.en: But he had to create a new way of thinking about something that existed in a new context.
sentences.zh: 但他必须创造出一种新的思路，把已经存在的东西放到一个全新的场景中去理解。

sentences.en: Which was its own innovation. And so, I think it's this interaction of true novelty--which is just fascinating how that can happen--and then this whole Lego-piece/combinatorial thing.
sentences.zh: 而这本身就是一种创新。所以我认为，正是真正的新颖性——这种事怎么会发生，实在令人着迷——和整套“乐高积木式”的组合逻辑之间的相互作用，成就了这一切。

sentences.en: But there's this last piece, and we'll close with this, which comes from a paper of William Baumol and rent-seeking, and how we should think about the wealth of nations, and where is it productive to spend your time in creating new products that help people or in creating new regulations that hamper your competitors?
sentences.zh: 但还有最后一块拼图，我们就以此作结——它来自威廉·鲍莫尔关于寻租的一篇论文，涉及我们该如何看待国民财富，以及把时间花在创造能帮助人们的新产品上、还是花在制定阻碍竞争对手的新规上，哪个才更具生产性？

sentences.en: And, when you read the story of the rollercoaster of Iqbal and Strive--what's his last name?
sentences.zh: 当你读到伊克巴尔和斯特赖夫这段跌宕起伏的故事——他姓什么来着？

sentences.en: Masiyiwa. Masiyiwa--you are forced to realize that the romantic story of the business person who has a vision--which they both did--and then forces the world, molds the world to accept that vision or brings that vision into reality through a set of decisions, maybe with a team of talented people, say, is only part of the story.
sentences.zh: 马西尤瓦。马西尤瓦——你会不得不意识到，那种关于商人怀揣远见——他们俩确实都有远见——然后强行让世界、塑造世界去接受这种远见，或者通过一系列决策、也许还有一支能干的团队，把这种远见变为现实的浪漫故事，其实只是故事的一部分。

sentences.en: Especially in poor countries with bad governance.
sentences.zh: 在治理糟糕的贫穷国家尤其如此。

sentences.en: Because, the temptations of rent-seeking to hamper innovators is so depressing and so important for understanding why certain countries stay poor.
sentences.zh: 因为，寻租行为对创新者的阻挠诱惑实在令人沮丧，而这对于理解为什么某些国家始终贫穷又至关重要。

sentences.en: And, it's really hard to remember how many setbacks there are, because you step back as an observer of, say, of Apple and you say, 'Yeah, well, Steve Jobs came up with this idea of a phone and he had to figure out a way to have a screen to enter the numbers.' Would it be like you'd punch a little keyboard or what?
sentences.zh: 而人们其实很难记住其中经历了多少挫折，因为当你作为一个旁观者去看苹果公司时，你会说：“是啊，史蒂夫·乔布斯想出了做手机这个点子，然后他得想办法弄出一块能输入号码的屏幕。”是不是会像敲一个小键盘那样？

sentences.en: Etc., etc. There are all these decisions that get made.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类，诸如此类。这中间要做出无数个决定。

sentences.en: But, as you say, Iqbal's not an innovator--excuse me--he's not a technologist.
sentences.zh: 但正如你说的，伊克巴尔并不是个创新者——抱歉，我是说，他不是个技术专家。

sentences.en: He's not an engineer or technologist. Not an engineer.
sentences.zh: 他既不是工程师，也不是技术专家。不是工程师。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly. Yeah. And yet, what he overcomes through persistence and drive to bring, help, ultimately lead to people in Bangladesh having more cell phones than people, is a part of the human experience and a part of the business world that is neglected--because it's not romantic, and it's depressing, and it's frustrating.
sentences.zh: 是啊，没错。是啊。然而，他凭借坚持不懈和拼劲所克服的种种困难，最终促成孟加拉国的手机数量超过了人口数量——这既是人类经历中被忽视的一部分，也是商业世界中被忽视的一部分——因为它并不浪漫，令人沮丧，也令人挫败。

sentences.en: And, it inevitably shows you the importance of persistence and drive as much as technology and vision of that kind, to bring things into the world that didn't exist before so that people can actually enjoy them and use them.
sentences.zh: 而这也不可避免地告诉我们，要把以前不存在的东西带到这个世界上、让人们真正能够享受它、使用它，坚持不懈和拼劲的重要性丝毫不亚于技术和那种远见。

sentences.en: Well, I think that's--I mean, you know what you're doing, so I'm not surprised, but I think that's a great place to close.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得这——我是说，你很清楚自己在做什么，所以我并不意外，但我觉得这是个很好的收尾点。

sentences.en: And so, there are a couple of things I think of real significance in what you just raised.
sentences.zh: 你刚才提出的这些内容里，有几点我觉得意义重大。

sentences.en: First of all, the Baumol paper.
sentences.zh: 首先是鲍莫尔那篇论文。

sentences.en: Actually, I have a collection of books that inspired me, and Baumol really was a very significant figure.
sentences.zh: 其实，我收藏了一批曾经启发过我的书，鲍莫尔确实是一位非常重要的人物。

sentences.en: This is Baumol's Microtheory of Entrepreneurship, recommended to everybody.
sentences.zh: 这本是鲍莫尔的《企业家精神微观理论》，推荐给每一个人。

sentences.en: But anyway, this specific paper of Baumol, it resolves a kind of an issue that I think a lot of people--general public type people--have with entrepreneurship, with elevating entrepreneurship.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，鲍莫尔这篇具体的论文，解决了一个我认为很多人——普通大众——对企业家精神、对推崇企业家精神抱有的疑虑。

sentences.en: Right? Intuitively, they kind of know something wrong with that picture, right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？他们凭直觉就能感觉到，这幅图景里似乎哪里不太对劲，对吧？

sentences.en: And Baumol--it goes directly at that. Human trafficking is entrepreneurship.
sentences.zh: 而鲍莫尔——他直接点出了问题所在。贩卖人口也是一种企业家行为。

sentences.en: And, I just read a great book about lobbying called The Wolves of K Street.
sentences.zh: 我刚读过一本关于游说行业的好书，叫《K街之狼》。

sentences.en: Right? That's entrepreneurship. Sure. It creates absolutely nothing and probably is net destructive, right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？那也是一种企业家行为。没错。它什么都没创造出来，甚至很可能是净破坏性的，对吧？

sentences.en: But, there's a lot of effort--and a lot of reward, a lot of financial incentive around that activity.
sentences.zh: 但围绕这类活动，投入了大量心力——也伴随着大量回报，大量的经济激励。

sentences.en: Sure. And, that is pure rent-seeking. And, it is entirely an artifact of the construction of the regulatory environment, the governance environment.
sentences.zh: 没错。而这纯粹就是寻租行为。它完全是监管环境、治理环境的建构方式所催生出的产物。

sentences.en: The fact that the state has the monopoly over the use of force, and that extends to a lot of other dimensions of economic and social life.
sentences.zh: 国家对暴力的使用拥有垄断权，而这种垄断延伸到了经济和社会生活的许多其他维度。

sentences.en: And so, there's a lot of ways that very creative, diligent, imaginative people can devote their efforts that are net destructive or, at best, indifferent to human wellbeing.
sentences.zh: 所以，那些极具创造力、勤奋且富有想象力的人，其实有很多种方式可以把精力投入到对人类福祉毫无益处、甚至是净破坏性的事情上去。

sentences.en: And, it's not at all guaranteed. I mean, another big question in entrepreneurship--and I don't have a really firm view on this; I don't think it's something that it's sensible to have a firm view on--is: Are entrepreneurs created or made?
sentences.zh: 这一点丝毫没有保证。我是说，企业家精神里还有另一个大问题——对此我并没有一个非常坚定的看法，我也不觉得对这个问题持有坚定看法是明智的——那就是：企业家究竟是天生的，还是后天造就的？

sentences.en: I mean, sorry, made-- Made or taught. Created or taught-- Made or taught, exactly-- Born or created.
sentences.zh: 我是说，抱歉，是造就的——是造就还是教出来的。是天生的还是教出来的——没错，是造就还是教出来的——是天生的还是被创造出来的。

sentences.en: Born or created. Whatever. Born or made.
sentences.zh: 天生的还是被创造出来的。随便怎么说吧。天生的还是造就的。

sentences.en: No: born or made. That's what it is. Born or made.
sentences.zh: 不对：是天生的还是造就的。就是这个说法。天生的还是造就的。

sentences.en: Everybody knows what we're talking about, but okay.
sentences.zh: 大家都明白我们在说什么，好吧，就这样。

sentences.en: Okay: Are entrepreneurs born or made? I don't particularly care.
sentences.zh: 好吧：企业家究竟是天生的还是后天造就的？我并不是特别在意这个问题。

sentences.en: I think they're at least partly made. There's some genetic aspect.
sentences.zh: 我认为至少有一部分是后天造就的。当然也有某种基因层面的因素。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter. But, Baumol really lands pretty hard on there's a certain subset of people that have these capabilities in any society.
sentences.zh: 这不重要。但鲍莫尔非常有力地指出：在任何社会中，总有一小部分人具备这些能力。

sentences.en: It's not everybody. And so, how the society is organized will determine whether they become involved in human trafficking, whether they go into lobbying or in some other ways rent-seeking activities, or whether they become creative entrepreneurs.
sentences.zh: 并非人人都具备。而社会的组织方式将决定，这些人最终是卷入人口贩卖，还是投身游说、或从事其他形式的寻租活动，抑或成为富有创造力的企业家。

sentences.en: And so, that's the one part of the institution story--the how nations fail story--that I buy.
sentences.zh: 所以，这正是“制度决定论”——也就是“国家为什么会失败”这套说法——里我认可的那一部分。

sentences.en: I mostly don't buy that at all. I mostly find-- You're talking about the-- Acemoglu and Robinson. the Robinson book-- Yeah.
sentences.zh: 但其余大部分我基本上并不认同。我基本上发现——你说的是——阿西莫格鲁和罗宾逊的书——对。

sentences.en: And, for a lot of the reasons that we just talked about, right?
sentences.zh: 原因很大程度上正是我们刚才聊到的那些，对吧？

sentences.en: I think it goes much, much too far in the institutional predestination direction and misses human agency almost entirely, at least as I read it.
sentences.zh: 我认为那本书在“制度决定命运”这个方向上走得太远太远了，几乎完全忽略了人的能动性——至少按我的理解是这样。

sentences.en: There's parts of the book that get into human agency, but I feel like it fails to resolve that.
sentences.zh: 书里确实有一部分涉及人的能动性，但我觉得它并没有真正把这个问题讲清楚。

sentences.en: So, but there is a piece of predestination, I think, that Baumol really hits on it.
sentences.zh: 不过，我认为确实存在一部分“注定”的因素，而鲍莫尔正好切中了这一点。

sentences.en: It's how entrepreneurs allocate their talent.
sentences.zh: 那就是企业家如何分配自己的才能。

sentences.en: And then, the second part of what you said-- It's the rules of the game.
sentences.zh: 然后是你刚才说的第二部分——那就是游戏规则。

sentences.en: You set up-- the rules of the game-- bad rules, you're going to encourage people to do bad things and-- you're going to encourage people to do bad things.
sentences.zh: 你制定的——游戏规则——如果规则不好，就会鼓励人们去做坏事——就会鼓励人们去做坏事。

sentences.en: It's just a piece of predestination with human agency layered on top of it.
sentences.zh: 这不过是在一部分“注定”的基础上，叠加了人的能动性。

sentences.en: So, now, as for the second part of what you just said, having to do with the centrality of persistence, of grit as we often sort of talk about in entrepreneurial success, as evidenced in particular in this book and the stories of Iqbal Quadir and Strive Masiyiwa, but also Nick Hughes and Susie Loney and M-PESA, and Shivani Siroya, who is more recently the founder of Tala--a great story.
sentences.zh: 那么，关于你刚才说的第二部分——关乎坚持、关乎我们常说的“毅力”在创业成功中的核心地位——这一点在这本书里，尤其是在伊克巴尔·夸德尔和斯特赖夫·马西尤瓦的故事里得到了印证，还有尼克·休斯和苏西·洛尼与M-PESA的故事，以及希瓦妮·西罗亚——她是较为晚近的Tala创始人——的故事，都是很棒的例子。

sentences.en: In every case, this determination. And, I feel like that's really the kind of takeaway from this book that I feel sort of resolves this born-or-made story about entrepreneurship.
sentences.zh: 每一个案例里，都是这种坚定的决心。我觉得这确实是这本书真正想传达的一个道理，也算是解决了“企业家究竟是天生还是后天造就”这个问题。

sentences.en: We can all be inspired by stories of people who have exceptional determination.
sentences.zh: 我们都可以从这些拥有非凡决心的人的故事中获得激励。

sentences.en: Right? And, Strive Masiyiwa, his initial idea--he left the country; he had the opportunity to study in England.
sentences.zh: 对吧？说到斯特赖夫·马西尤瓦，他最初的想法是——他离开了祖国，有机会去英国求学。

sentences.en: And there was a revolution going on to overthrow the white supremacist government in Rhodesia.
sentences.zh: 当时罗得西亚正爆发一场革命，要推翻白人至上主义政府。

sentences.en: And, a cousin of his was part of that, and he said, 'I'm going to come back and fight in the revolution,' as he was doing with Mugabe and his allies.
sentences.zh: 他的一个堂兄参与了这场革命，他说：“我要回国参加革命去打仗”，就像他和穆加贝及其盟友们一起做的那样。

sentences.en: And, the cousin said, 'We're going to win.
sentences.zh: 而堂兄却说：“我们肯定会赢的。

sentences.en: Don't do that. You'll probably just get killed.
sentences.zh: 你别回来。你多半只会白白送命。

sentences.en: Stay in England and study something that will be useful after we win.'And so, Masiyiwa gets a degree in engineering.
sentences.zh: 留在英国，好好学点等我们赢了之后用得上的东西。”于是，马西尤瓦拿到了工程学学位。

sentences.en: And so, you think the story is going to be he comes back and starts a mobile phone company.
sentences.zh: 于是你会以为，接下来的故事就是他回国后创办了一家手机公司。

sentences.en: But no, that's not the story. The story is that he comes back and gets a job in the government telecommunications monopoly, because that's the only jobs that exist.
sentences.zh: 但不，事实并非如此。真实的故事是，他回国后在政府垄断的电信公司找了份工作，因为当时能找到的工作也就只有这一种。

sentences.en: And then, you think he's going to leave that and start a mobile phone company, but that's not the story.
sentences.zh: 接下来你又会以为，他会辞掉这份工作去创办手机公司，但事实也不是这样。

sentences.en: He wants to build a house and he gets a loan for the house, but the quotes he gets for the construction are twice the amount of the loan.
sentences.zh: 他想盖一栋房子，为此申请了一笔贷款，但施工方给出的报价却是贷款金额的两倍。

sentences.en: So, in order to manage the project himself, he has to create a company.
sentences.zh: 所以，为了能自己接手这个项目，他不得不成立一家公司。

sentences.en: That's the only way. He has to actually create a company in order to get around these extremely high construction bids.
sentences.zh: 这是唯一的办法。他必须真的成立一家公司，才能绕开这些高得离谱的施工报价。

sentences.en: So, that company becomes very successful.
sentences.zh: 结果这家公司变得非常成功。

sentences.en: It's a construction business--has nothing to do with telecommunications.
sentences.zh: 这是一家建筑公司——和电信业毫无关系。

sentences.en: And then, out of that, he creates Econet.
sentences.zh: 然后，正是从这家公司出发，他创办了Econet。

sentences.en: And then he runs into one obstacle. He runs into another obstacle.
sentences.zh: 然后他遇到了一个障碍。接着又遇到了另一个障碍。

sentences.en: He's abducted and threatened. There's all these stories.
sentences.zh: 他被绑架、被威胁。这样的故事还有很多很多。

sentences.en: Ultimately, he first sues the government--and loses--and then he appeals to the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 最终，他先是起诉了政府——败诉了——然后又上诉到最高法院。

sentences.en: He appeals to the Supreme Court on constitutional basis.
sentences.zh: 他以宪法为依据向最高法院上诉。

sentences.en: So, he not only sues the Mugabe government and loses, he actually makes a constitutional case that it is a right of the people of Zimbabwe to have telecommunication services.
sentences.zh: 所以，他不仅起诉了穆加贝政府并败诉，还实实在在地提出了一个宪法层面的主张：拥有电信服务是津巴布韦人民的一项权利。

sentences.en: And, the heroes of this story actually is the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 而这个故事真正的英雄，其实是最高法院。

sentences.en: It shows the importance of an independent judiciary, because over and over the Supreme Court ultimately rules in his favor.
sentences.zh: 这也说明了独立司法的重要性，因为最高法院一次又一次地最终裁定他胜诉。

sentences.en: That's why he's able to succeed. But it's just part of the story.
sentences.zh: 这正是他最终能够成功的原因。但这也只是故事的一部分。

sentences.en: It goes on and on. I mean, the amount of determination.
sentences.zh: 故事还在继续。我是说，这需要何等的决心。

sentences.en: And, he enlists his evangelical colleagues.
sentences.zh: 他还招募了自己福音派教会里的同僚们。

sentences.en: He gets ministers who are in Zimbabwe in conversion missions that actually sign up for Econet service even though it doesn't exist yet, to kind of subsidize.
sentences.zh: 他找到那些正在津巴布韦传教的牧师们，让他们在Econet服务尚未真正开通之前就提前注册使用，相当于给这项服务提供一种补贴。

sentences.en: And, his students showing up--4,000 students show up in protest, in favor of Strive Masiyiwa because it's really part of the second stage of independence.
sentences.zh: 而他的学生们也挺身而出——四千名学生走上街头抗议，力挺斯特赖夫·马西尤瓦，因为这实实在在是“第二阶段独立”的一部分。

sentences.en: It's the personal, the market independence.
sentences.zh: 那是一种个人层面的、市场层面的独立。

sentences.en: They've received independence from white supremacists, but now they have to create that internal independence.
sentences.zh: 他们已经从白人至上主义者手中赢得了独立，但现在他们还必须创造出那种内在的独立。

sentences.en: So, this--what are we going to do? What are we going to do when we wake up in the morning in a reality where so much is predetermined, so much seems out of our control?
sentences.zh: 所以，这——我们该怎么办？当我们早上醒来，面对这样一个现实——太多事情早已被注定，太多事情看似不受我们掌控——我们又该怎么办？

sentences.en: And, what this book says to me, what these stories--that I did not create.
sentences.zh: 而这本书对我诉说的、这些我并未凭空创造出来的故事——

sentences.en: I didn't create the stories in this book.
sentences.zh: 这本书里的故事，都不是我创造出来的。

sentences.en: They were lived by other people. It's a nonfiction book.
sentences.zh: 它们是别人真实经历过的人生。这是一本纪实类的书。

sentences.en: I discovered the stories and I did my best to tell them.
sentences.zh: 我只是发现了这些故事，并尽我所能把它们讲述出来。

sentences.en: So, when I say that they're great stories, I didn't create them.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我说这些是了不起的故事时，创造它们的人并不是我。

sentences.en: Right? I mean, I just identified them and tried to relate them.
sentences.zh: 对吧？我是说，我只是发现了它们，并试着把它们转述出来。

sentences.en: And they are great stories; and they're great stories about how we actually make a difference.
sentences.zh: 而它们确实是了不起的故事；是关于我们究竟如何能带来真正改变的了不起的故事。

sentences.en: What we do makes a difference. It can make a difference, it will make a difference.
sentences.zh: 我们的所作所为是有意义的。它可以带来改变，它也终将带来改变。

sentences.en: What will be is not predetermined. We play a role, small and large, and I truly believe that.
sentences.zh: 未来会是什么样，并非早已注定。我们都在其中扮演着或大或小的角色，我是真心相信这一点的。

sentences.en: And I think it is a deep misunderstanding of history, philosophy, religion, and certainly economics to believe otherwise.
sentences.zh: 我认为，如果不这样相信，那就是对历史、哲学、宗教，当然还有经济学，存在着一种深刻的误解。

sentences.en: That's really the point of this book. But, I would just add that we make a difference, but poor Strive Masiyiwa could have made a much bigger difference if he lived in a country that didn't try to crush him to enable Mugabe in order to enrich his cronies.
sentences.zh: 这确实正是这本书的核心观点。不过，我想补充一点：我们确实能带来改变，但可怜的斯特赖夫·马西尤瓦本可以带来大得多的改变，如果他所在的国家没有试图打压他、以此讨好穆加贝、方便他中饱私囊那帮亲信的话。

sentences.en: So, it's a tragedy that a man of that talent had to devote so much of it to being allowed to do what he could do.
sentences.zh: 所以说，这真是一场悲剧——一个如此有才华的人，竟不得不把大量才干耗费在“争取获准去做他本可以做的事”这件事本身上。

sentences.en: I just want to add one thing to that. Yeah, please.
sentences.zh: 我想再补充一点。好，请说。

sentences.en: It's an interesting thing, because years, years ago--I mean probably early 2000s--I was with Iqbal and the engineers from Telenor that had helped Grameenphone come into being.
sentences.zh: 这事挺有意思的，因为很多很多年前——我是说大概是2000年代初——我曾经和伊克巴尔，以及帮助Grameenphone成立的Telenor公司的工程师们在一起。

sentences.en: And this was just after Iqbal--just as Iqbal was exiting Grameenphone.
sentences.zh: 那正是在伊克巴尔——就在伊克巴尔即将退出Grameenphone的时候。

sentences.en: So he still was part of the company. And, I said this, I was, like, 'It's incredible that you were able to achieve what you did in the environment that you did.' I mean, and both of them--both the Telenor folks and Iqbal--said, 'Well, actually in some ways it was easier.
sentences.zh: 所以他当时还是公司的一员。我当时说：“你们能在那样的环境下取得这样的成就，真是不可思议。”结果他们俩——Telenor那边的人和伊克巴尔——都说：“其实从某些方面来说，反倒更容易一些。

sentences.en: I don't think we ever could have done what we did with Grameenphone in the United States.
sentences.zh: 我们不觉得，我们做Grameenphone这件事，要是放在美国，还能做成。

sentences.en: Because everything was unregulated.'The way that you know that Strive Masiyiwa and Iqbal Quadir were first, was that they didn't pay for the licenses.
sentences.zh: 因为那边什么都没有监管。”而你能知道斯特赖夫·马西尤瓦和伊克巴尔·夸德尔确实是第一批入局者的一个方式，就是他们当初根本没为牌照付过钱。

sentences.en: Within years--within just a few years--the licenses spectrum for mobile telephony, even in poor countries, was going in the tens and hundreds of millions of dollars.
sentences.zh: 而就在几年之内——短短几年之内——移动通信的频谱牌照，即便是在贫穷国家，价格也已经飙升到了数千万乃至数亿美元。

sentences.en: Right? Mo Ibrahim became a billionaire by aggregating those licenses--that instantly become very valuable once the market test was passed.
sentences.zh: 对吧？穆·易卜拉欣正是靠着大量收购这些牌照才成为亿万富翁的——这些牌照一旦通过了市场检验，价值瞬间就变得极高。

sentences.en: But, in Bangladesh, it was just a question of: Yes, there was a bidding process, but the licenses themselves were given away because nobody thought that they were worth anything.
sentences.zh: 但在孟加拉国，情况只是这样：没错，确实有过招标流程，但牌照本身几乎是白送出去的，因为当时根本没人觉得它们值什么钱。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I mean, there was something about this absolute lack of appreciation of what the possibilities would be that allowed them to bring together the resources in a way that in a regulated environment would be very difficult.
sentences.zh: 所以，是啊，我是说，正是因为当时完全没人意识到其中蕴藏的可能性，才让他们得以以一种在受严格监管的环境里根本难以实现的方式，把各种资源整合到了一起。

sentences.en: So, in some ways, entrepreneurs in a place like the United States have a harder time, because the incumbent power is so entrenched or at least can be, and regulations are so well-defined.
sentences.zh: 所以从某些方面来说，像美国这样的地方，企业家反而更不容易，因为既得利益势力根深蒂固——至少有可能如此——而各项监管规则也界定得如此清晰。

sentences.en: All the building and other restrictions that we talked about that are very significant.
sentences.zh: 我们之前提到的所有建设限制以及其他各种限制，影响都非常重大。

sentences.en: So, it's not totally clear that it's harder in these environments that we live in.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们如今所生活的这类环境是不是就一定更难做成事，其实也并不那么绝对。

sentences.en: My guest today has been Philip Auerswald.
sentences.zh: 今天的嘉宾是菲利普·奥尔斯瓦德。

sentences.en: His book is A Phone Is a Cow. Philip, thanks for being part of EconTalk.
sentences.zh: 他的著作是《手机就是一头牛》。菲利普，谢谢你做客EconTalk。

sentences.en: It's been a real pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这真是一段非常愉快的时光。
